entries.title: How to Sign In to HRISense
entries.text:
Open HRISense and sign in with your email and password.
Purpose: Open your HRISense account using the email address and password HR gave you.
When to use: At the start of your shift, or any time you need to open HRISense on a hospital computer or your own device.
Before you start: HR has created your HRISense account and given you a temporary password.; Your computer or phone can reach the HRISense address used by the hospital.
Step 1. Open the sign-in page: Open your web browser and go to the HRISense address. If you try to open any other HRISense page while signed out, you are taken to the sign-in page automatically. (Where: Web browser -> HRISense address. Result: The Sign in to HRISense screen appears, with an Email box and a Password box.)
Step 2. Type your email and password: Type your personal email — the one HR recorded as your login — in **Personal email**, then type your password in **Password**. (Where: Sign-in card -> Email and Password. Tip: Check that Caps Lock is off before typing your password.. Result: Both boxes are filled in.)
Step 3. Decide whether to stay signed in: Tick **Keep me signed in** only if this is your own device. Leave it unticked on a shared hospital computer. (Where: Sign-in card -> Keep me signed in. Warning: On a shared computer, leave this unticked. Otherwise the next person to open the browser could reach your account.. Result: The tick box shows your choice.)
Step 4. Select Sign In: Tick **I'm not a robot** if it is shown, then select **Sign In to HRISense**. Until the box is ticked, the button reads **Please finish the CAPTCHA** and cannot be selected. (Where: Sign-in card -> Sign In to HRISense. Tip: If **Continue with Google** is shown, you can use it instead of steps 2 and 4 — but only with the Google account whose email is the same personal email HR registered. It never creates an account, and a temporary password must still be changed first.. Result: Your dashboard opens. If this is your first sign-in, you are asked to set your own password first.)
What happens next: You land on the dashboard for your role, and the menu on the left shows the parts of HRISense you may use.
Problem: It says "Invalid email or password". — Solution: Check the spelling of your email and make sure Caps Lock is off. If you still cannot get in, select "Forgot password?" on the sign-in page.
Problem: It takes me to a Change Password screen instead of the dashboard. — Solution: That is normal for a new or reset account. Set your own password and you will continue straight to the dashboard.
Problem: The button says "Please finish the CAPTCHA". — Solution: Tick **I'm not a robot** above the button (and complete the picture check if Google shows one). The box is needed for every sign-in, and again after each failed attempt.
Problem: The button says "Try again in …" after a wrong password. — Solution: Each wrong password makes this browser wait before the next try: 15 seconds, then 30 seconds, then 1 minute, then 15 minutes for every further wrong password. Your account itself is never locked by wrong passwords, so you can still sign in from another device. A successful sign-in resets the waits; otherwise they are forgotten after an hour without failures.
Problem: It says my account is locked. — Solution: HR Personnel locked the account on purpose (for example for a security concern). Ask them to unlock it.
Problem: It says my account is inactive. — Solution: Ask HR Personnel to check your account. Deactivated accounts cannot sign in until HR reactivates them.
Problem: Continue with Google says no HRISense account is registered with this Google email. — Solution: Google sign-in only works when your Google email is exactly the personal email HR recorded for you. Sign in with your email and password, or ask HR to check which email is on your account. Do not keep trying other Google accounts: repeated attempts with unregistered emails block Google sign-in on your network for a while.
Problem: It says Google sign-in is blocked on this network. — Solution: Someone on your network tried Google sign-in with unregistered emails several times. Sign in with your email and password — that still works — and Google sign-in comes back on its own after about 30 minutes.
Problem: Nothing happens when I select Continue with Google. — Solution: Your browser may be blocking pop-ups. Allow pop-ups for the HRISense address and try again, or sign in with your email and password.
Tip: Always sign out when you leave a shared hospital computer.
Tip: Save the HRISense address as a browser bookmark so it is quick to open.

entries.title: Using "Keep Me Signed In"
entries.text:
What the Keep me signed in tick box does, and when it is safe to use.
Purpose: Decide whether HRISense should keep you signed in after you close the browser.
When to use: Every time you sign in. The choice matters most on shared hospital workstations.
Before you start: You are on the HRISense sign-in page.
Step 1. Find the tick box: Underneath the Password box you will see **Keep me signed in**. (Where: Sign-in card -> Keep me signed in. When ticked, your session stays open after you close the browser. When unticked, closing the browser ends your session.. Result: You can see the tick box before you select Sign In.)
Step 2. Choose based on the device: Tick it on a device only you use. Leave it unticked on any shared computer, including nurse stations and office workstations used by several staff. (Where: Sign-in card -> Keep me signed in. Warning: Never tick this on a shared computer. Anyone who opens the browser afterwards would be inside your account, including your own records.. Result: HRISense remembers your choice for the next time you sign in on this device.)
What happens next: If you ticked it, you will usually go straight to your dashboard the next time you open HRISense on that device. If you left it unticked, you will be asked to sign in again.
Problem: I ticked it but I still have to sign in again. — Solution: Sessions do expire after a period of inactivity, and clearing browser data ends them too. Simply sign in again.
Problem: I ticked it by mistake on a shared computer. — Solution: Sign out from the profile menu at the top right. Signing out clears the saved session on that computer.
Tip: If you are not sure whether a computer is shared, leave the box unticked.

entries.title: Setting Your Password on First Sign-In
entries.text:
Replace the temporary password HR gave you with one only you know.
Purpose: Replace the temporary password issued by HR with a password that only you know.
When to use: The first time you sign in, and any time HR resets your password for you.
Before you start: You have the temporary password from your welcome email, or HR gave it to you directly.; You have signed in with that temporary password.
Step 1. Sign in with the temporary password: Sign in as normal with your personal email (the one HR registered) and the temporary password. (Where: Sign-in page -> Sign In to HRISense. HRISense knows the password is temporary and takes you straight to **Change Your Temporary Password**, which shows your registered email (partly hidden). Nothing else in HRISense opens until you set your own password — not even by typing another address.. Result: The Change Your Temporary Password screen appears instead of your dashboard.)
Step 2. Enter your temporary password and your new one: Type the temporary password in **Current Temporary Password**. Type your new password in **New Password**, then type the same password again in **Confirm New Password**. (Where: Change Password screen. A checklist under the New Password box shows the rules. Every rule must be ticked before you can continue.. Warning: Your new password must be different from the temporary one.. Result: All the rules in the checklist turn green and the button becomes available.)
Step 3. Save the new password: Select **Set New Password & Continue**. (Where: Change Password screen -> Set New Password & Continue. Result: Your dashboard opens. From now on you sign in with the new password.)
What happens next: The temporary password stops working immediately. Use your new password from now on. If you were also signed in on another computer or phone, that one is signed out and needs the new password. Not ready yet? Select **Sign out** on the same screen.
Problem: The save button stays greyed out. — Solution: Look at the checklist under the New Password box. Every rule must be met, and the two new password boxes must match exactly.
Problem: It says the current password is wrong. — Solution: Type the temporary password carefully — it is easy to confuse letter O with the number 0. If it still fails, ask HR Personnel to issue a new one.
Problem: I never received the welcome email. — Solution: Check your junk or spam folder first. The welcome email goes to your personal email address. If it is not there, ask HR Personnel to send new credentials.
Tip: Choose something you can remember but others cannot guess. Do not use your birthday or your employee number.
Tip: Never write your password on a note left at your workstation.

entries.title: How to Change Your Password
entries.text:
Change the password of an account you are already signed in to.
Purpose: Set a new password while you are signed in, for regular security housekeeping.
When to use: When you think someone may have seen your password, or when you simply want to change it.
Before you start: You are signed in and you know your current password.; Your new password must be at least 8 characters and include an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number, and a special character.
Step 1. Open Settings: Select **Settings** in the menu on the left, or open the profile menu at the top right and choose **Settings**. In the **Security** card, select **Change password**. (Where: Settings -> Security -> Change password. Result: The Security card shows Current password, New password and Confirm new password boxes.)
Step 2. Fill in the three boxes: Type your existing password in **Current password**, then your new password in **New password** and again in **Confirm new password**. (Where: Settings -> Security. The checklist shows which password rules you have met so far.. Result: The checklist is fully ticked and the update button becomes available.)
Step 3. Save: Select **Update password**. (Where: Settings -> Security -> Update password. HRISense checks your current password before saving, so nobody can change your password from a computer you left open without knowing it.. Result: A confirmation message appears. The new password works immediately.)
What happens next: Use the new password the next time you sign in.
Problem: It says my current password is incorrect. — Solution: Type it again carefully. If you cannot remember it, sign out and use "Forgot password?" on the sign-in page.
Problem: It says the new password must be different from the current one. — Solution: Choose a password you are not already using. Reusing the same password is not allowed.
Tip: Changing your password does not affect any of your records — only how you sign in.

entries.title: What to Do If You Forgot Your Password
entries.text:
Ask HRISense to email you a link so you can set a new password yourself.
Purpose: Get back into your account when you cannot remember your password, without waiting for HR.
When to use: When the sign-in page keeps refusing your password and you are sure your email is correct.
Before you start: You know the email address your HRISense account uses.; You can open that mailbox.
Step 1. Select "Forgot password?": On the sign-in page, select **Forgot password?** underneath the Password box. (Where: Sign-in page -> Forgot password?. Result: The Forgot Password page opens with a single email box.)
Step 2. Type your email address and send: Type the email address your account uses, tick **I'm not a robot** if it is shown, and select **Send reset link**. (Where: Forgot Password page -> Send reset link. For safety, HRISense always shows the same confirmation message, whether or not the address belongs to an account. That way nobody can use this page to discover who has an account.. Result: A message confirms that if the address belongs to an account, a reset link has been sent to it.)
Step 3. Open the link in your email: Open the message from HRISense and select **Choose a new password**. Follow the Reset Your Password guide from there. (Where: Email -> Choose a new password. Warning: The link expires after a short time, and it can only be used once. If it has expired, simply request a new one.. Result: The Reset Password page opens in your browser.)
What happens next: Once you set a new password you can sign in with it straight away. Your old password stops working.
Problem: No email arrived. — Solution: Wait a few minutes and check your junk or spam folder. Make sure you typed the address your account actually uses. If nothing arrives, ask HR Personnel to reset your password for you.
Problem: The link says it is invalid or has expired. — Solution: Request a new reset link from the sign-in page. Each link can only be used once.
Tip: If you are in a hurry, HR Personnel can issue new credentials immediately from your employee record.

entries.title: Setting a New Password from the Emailed Link
entries.text:
Finish a password reset using the link HRISense emailed you.
Purpose: Set a brand-new password using the one-time link sent to your email.
When to use: Right after you request a reset link from the sign-in page.
Before you start: You have the reset email in front of you.; The link has not expired and has not already been used.
Step 1. Open the link: Select **Choose a new password** in the email, or copy the address shown underneath the button into your browser. (Where: Email -> Choose a new password. Result: The Reset Password page opens.)
Step 2. Type your new password twice: Type the new password in **New Password**, then again in **Confirm New Password**. (Where: Reset Password page. The checklist shows the rules your password must meet.. Result: The checklist is fully ticked.)
Step 3. Save and sign in: Select **Set new password**, then sign in with the password you just chose. (Where: Reset Password page -> Set new password. Result: A confirmation appears and you are returned to the sign-in page.)
What happens next: The reset link is used up and cannot be opened again. Your new password works immediately.
Problem: The page says the link is no longer valid. — Solution: Request a new one with "Forgot password?" on the sign-in page. Links expire and can only be used once.
Problem: The save button will not turn on. — Solution: Check the rules checklist and make sure both password boxes match exactly.
Tip: If you did not ask for a reset, you can ignore the email — your password is unchanged. Tell HR Personnel if it keeps happening.

entries.title: How to Sign Out Safely
entries.text:
End your session properly, especially on a shared hospital computer.
Purpose: Close your HRISense session so nobody else can use your account.
When to use: Every time you finish working on a shared computer, and whenever you step away from your desk.
Before you start: You are signed in to HRISense.
Step 1. Open your profile menu: Select your name or photo at the top right of the screen. (Where: Top bar -> your name. Result: A short menu appears with My Profile, Settings and Sign Out.)
Step 2. Select Sign Out: Select **Sign Out**. (Where: Profile menu -> Sign Out. HRISense closes your session on this device. Simply closing the browser tab is not the same thing.. Result: You are returned to the sign-in page.)
What happens next: Anyone who opens HRISense on that computer afterwards has to sign in with their own account.
Problem: I closed the browser without signing out on a shared computer. — Solution: Sign in again on that computer and sign out properly. If you had ticked "Keep me signed in", this is the only way to clear the saved session.
Tip: Signing out on one computer does not sign you out on your other devices.

entries.title: How to Sign In with Google
entries.text:
Use Continue with Google instead of typing your password — only with the Google account that uses your registered email.
Purpose: Sign in to your own HRISense account through Google, without typing your HRISense password.
When to use: When **Continue with Google** appears on the sign-in page and your Google account uses the same email HR registered for you.
Before you start: HR has already created your HRISense account. Google sign-in never creates an account.; Your Google account email is exactly the personal email HR recorded as your login.; Your browser allows pop-ups for the HRISense address.
Step 1. Choose whether to stay signed in: On the sign-in page, tick **Keep me signed in** only if this is your own device. (Where: Sign-in page -> Keep me signed in. Result: The tick box shows your choice. It works the same way as for a password sign-in.)
Step 2. Select Continue with Google: Under the **Sign In to HRISense** button, select **Continue with Google**, then pick your Google account in the Google window. (Where: Sign-in page -> Continue with Google. If you close the Google window, nothing happens — you can simply try again or sign in with your password.. Result: The Google window closes and HRISense signs you in.)
Step 3. Continue as usual: You land on your dashboard. If your account still has a temporary password, HRISense first asks you to set your own password, exactly as with a normal sign-in. (Where: Dashboard. Result: You are signed in with the same access you always have.)
What happens next: You use HRISense exactly as after a password sign-in. Your access comes from your HRISense account, never from Google.
Problem: It says no HRISense account is registered with this Google email. — Solution: Your Google email is not the personal email on your HRISense account. Sign in with your email and password, or ask HR which email is registered. Do not keep trying other Google accounts — repeated attempts with unregistered emails block Google sign-in on your network for a while.
Problem: It says Google sign-in is blocked on this network. — Solution: Several unregistered Google accounts were tried from your network. Sign in with your email and password; Google sign-in comes back after about 30 minutes.
Problem: It says my account is locked or deactivated. — Solution: Google sign-in follows the same account rules as a password. Ask HR Personnel to unlock a locked account or reactivate a deactivated one.
Problem: I do not see Continue with Google. — Solution: Google sign-in is switched on by HRISense administrators. If it is not shown, sign in with your email and password.
Tip: Signing out of HRISense does not sign you out of Google on that computer. On a shared computer, sign out of Google too.

entries.title: Navigating the HR Dashboard
entries.text:
Headcount, compliance follow-ups, leave awaiting your decision, and the attendance trend.
Purpose: See at a glance what needs HR attention today.
When to use: At the start of the day, or whenever you return to HRISense.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel (HR Officer, HR staff or Sister).
Step 1. Open the dashboard: Select **Dashboard** at the top of the menu. It is also the page you land on after signing in. Current announcements are shown first. (Where: Left menu -> Dashboard. Result: The welcome panel shows your summary cards.)
Step 2. Read the summary cards: Check **Total Employees**, **Compliance: Action Required** (missing, expired or expiring records), **Compliance: Needs Review** (submitted records waiting for HR) and **Awaiting HR Decision** (leave requests waiting for you). (Where: Dashboard -> summary cards. Result: You know which module needs you first.)
Step 3. Check the attendance trend: The **Attendance Trend** chart shows the monthly attendance rate from imported attendance records. Select **View breakdown** to see each month's counts. (Where: Dashboard -> Attendance Trend -> View breakdown. A day with no imported record is never counted as an absence. Months with no imported attendance show no rate instead of zero.. Result: You can see how each month's rate was worked out.)
Step 4. Use your calendar and activity: Below the chart is **My Calendar** (holidays, leave, trainings, interviews, deadlines, birthdays and notes). On the right, **Recent Activity** lists what you did in HRISense. (Where: Dashboard -> My Calendar / Recent Activity. Result: You can plan the day and retrace your own recent actions.)
What happens next: Open any module from the menu, or use **Quick actions** (the ⚡ button in the top bar) for common HR tasks.
Problem: The attendance chart says "No attendance data yet". — Solution: No attendance has been imported. The chart appears once attendance records are imported from the biometric export.
Problem: There is no To Do list on my dashboard. — Solution: That is intentional for HR: you work from the module pages, such as Leave Requests and Compliance.
Tip: Selecting the HRISense logo at the top left brings you back to the dashboard from anywhere.

entries.title: Navigating the Supervisor Dashboard
entries.text:
Your team count, team compliance, who is in today, and what is waiting on you.
Purpose: Check on the staff who report to you and pick up what is waiting for your action.
When to use: At the start of your shift.
Before you start: You are signed in as a Head, Supervisor or Coordinator.; HR has recorded you as the immediate supervisor of your staff.
Step 1. Open the dashboard: Select **Dashboard** in the menu. Current announcements are shown first. (Where: Left menu -> Dashboard. Result: The welcome panel shows your team cards.)
Step 2. Read the team cards: Check **Team Count** (your direct reports), **Team Compliance: Action Required**, **Team Compliance: Needs Review** and **Late Today**. (Where: Dashboard -> team cards. Only staff whose immediate supervisor is you are counted — not everyone in your unit.. Result: You see your team's standing for today.)
Step 3. See who is in: Read **Team Presence Today** and **Late & Tardiness Log Monitoring**. Select **View All Records** to open Daily Monitoring. (Where: Dashboard -> Team Presence Today. These show the attendance that has been imported. A team member with no imported record is not shown as absent.. Result: You know who has an attendance record today.)
Step 4. Work through your To Do list: On the right, **To Do** lists what is waiting on you — for example leave to endorse or an evaluation to complete. Select an item to open it. **Hide** removes an item from the list; **Show hidden** brings hidden items back. (Where: Dashboard -> To Do. Result: Each task opens the page where you complete it.)
What happens next: Leave you endorse goes on to HR for the final decision.
Problem: My team looks empty or someone is missing. — Solution: Your team is the staff whose immediate supervisor is you. Ask HR to check the supervisor recorded on that person's profile.
Tip: Use **Quick actions** (⚡ in the top bar) to jump to My Team, Leave Requests or Team Attendance.

entries.title: Navigating Your Dashboard
entries.text:
Your leave balances, weekly schedule, requirements and the things waiting on you.
Purpose: See your own work information in one place.
When to use: Whenever you sign in.
Before you start: You are signed in to HRISense.
Step 1. Open the dashboard: Select **Dashboard** in the menu. It is where you land after signing in. Announcements for you are shown first. (Where: Left menu -> Dashboard. Result: The welcome panel shows your requirement cards.)
Step 2. Check your requirements: Read **My Requirements: Action Required** (missing or expired), **Expiring Soon** and **Awaiting HR Review** (submitted, not yet reviewed). (Where: Dashboard -> requirement cards. Result: You know whether any requirement needs your attention.)
Step 3. Check your leave and your week: **Your Leave Balances** shows the days available to file for each leave type; select **View breakdown** to see allotted, used, pending and forfeited days. **Weekly Work Schedule** shows this week's shifts. (Where: Dashboard -> Your Leave Balances / Weekly Work Schedule. Result: You know how many days you can file and when you work.)
Step 4. Use your To Do list and calendar: **To Do** on the right lists what is waiting on you, such as an evaluation to complete. **My Calendar** shows holidays, your leave, trainings, deadlines and your notes. (Where: Dashboard -> To Do / My Calendar. Result: Selecting a To Do item opens the page where you complete it.)
What happens next: You can file leave, open **My Profile** or check your attendance from the menu or from **Quick actions** (⚡ in the top bar).
Problem: My schedule panel is empty. — Solution: A weekly schedule has not been set for you yet. Ask your supervisor or HR.
Problem: My leave balance looks wrong. — Solution: Vacation, Sick, Bereavement, Paternity and Solo Parent balances follow your completed years of service; other balances are entered by HR. Open **View breakdown**, or your profile's Leave tab, to see how each figure was reached, and contact HR if it still looks wrong.
Tip: The bell at the top right shows notifications addressed to you.

entries.title: How to Use My Calendar and Notes
entries.text:
See holidays, leave, trainings and deadlines on your dashboard calendar, and keep your own notes.
Purpose: Plan your days from one calendar and keep short notes for yourself.
When to use: When you want to see what is coming up, or jot down a reminder for a date.
Before you start: You are signed in to HRISense.
Step 1. Open My Calendar: On your **Dashboard**, scroll to **My Calendar**. Switch between **Day**, **Week** and **Month**, and use **Show:** to choose which kinds of entries appear. (Where: Dashboard -> My Calendar. It combines approved holidays, leave, trainings you are part of, deadlines, birthdays (HR: everyone's; supervisors: their team's), interviews (HR) and notes — only what you are allowed to see.. Result: The calendar shows the entries you chose.)
Step 2. Add a note: Pick a date, type a title (and optional details), and select **Add Note**. (Where: My Calendar -> Add Note. A note you add is private: it is marked **Only you**.. Result: The note appears on that date.)
Step 3. Mark it done, edit or delete it: Tick a note to mark it done (untick to reopen). Use the edit button and **Save** to change it, or delete it. (Where: My Calendar -> note. Result: Done notes are crossed out; overdue ones are flagged.)
What happens next: **Recent Activity**, on the right of the dashboard, lists what you did in HRISense, newest first. Only you see it; use **Show activity as of a date** to look further back.
Problem: I cannot edit a note someone posted to me. — Solution: Only the person who wrote a note can change or remove it.
Tip: Your private notes are never shown to HR or anyone else.

entries.title: How to Post a Calendar Note to Employees (HR)
entries.text:
Put a note on everyone's calendar, or on selected employees' calendars, with a notification.
Purpose: Remind staff of a date — for example a fire drill — on their own calendars.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.
Step 1. Open Post to employees: On your dashboard, in **My Calendar**, select **Post to employees**. (Where: Dashboard -> My Calendar -> Post to employees. Result: The "Post a note to employees" window opens.)
Step 2. Choose who sees it and post: Choose **All employees** or **Selected employees** (search and pick them), enter the date, title and optional details, and post it. (Where: Post a note to employees -> post. Result: The note shows as posted to everyone or to the people you picked, and each recipient gets a notification.)
What happens next: Only you can edit or remove the note. Removing it takes it off everyone's calendar.
Problem: It says to choose at least one employee. — Solution: With **Selected employees**, pick at least one person.
Tip: For a formal notice with read tracking, use Announcements instead.

entries.title: How to Search and Filter the Employee Directory
entries.text:
Find a staff member by name, ID, job role, unit or department, filter the list, and export it.
Purpose: Locate an employee record quickly, or produce a list of staff.
When to use: Whenever you need to open someone's record or review a group of staff.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel. The Employee Directory is HR's screen; supervisors use **My Team** and everyone uses **My Profile**.
Step 1. Open the directory: In the menu, open **Employees** and select **All Employees**. (Where: Left menu -> Employees -> All Employees. Result: The directory lists active employees with their state, job role, unit, supervisor and profile completion.)
Step 2. Search: Type part of a name, employee ID, job role, unit or department in the search box. (Where: Employee Directory -> search. Result: The list narrows as you type.)
Step 3. Filter the list: Use the state buttons (for example Active or On Leave) and the **Pending Assignment** filter for staff without a confirmed supervisor. Open **Advanced Directory Filters** for **Unit**, **Department**, **Job Role**, **Account Status**, **Record Scope** (active, archived or both) and **Hired From / Hired To**. (Where: Employee Directory -> filters. Result: Only matching employees remain.)
Step 4. Export or adjust the columns (optional): Use the export button to download the current page, the selected rows or every matching employee as Excel, PDF or CSV. **Toggle Columns** chooses which columns show. (Where: Employee Directory -> export / Toggle Columns. Result: The file downloads with the employees you chose.)
What happens next: Select a row to open that employee's profile in Employee Management.
Problem: I cannot find someone I know works here. — Solution: Clear the search and filters. If the person has left, set **Record Scope** to include archived employees, or open **Archived Employees**.
Tip: Select a profile completion figure to see what is missing from that 201 file.

entries.title: How to Onboard a New Employee (201 Setup)
entries.text:
Complete the eight-step wizard that creates the 201 file and the login account.
Purpose: Register a newly hired staff member, create their 201 file, and issue their HRISense login.
When to use: When a new employee joins Hospicio de San Jose and needs a record and an account.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; You have the employee's personal details, personal email (it becomes their login), mobile number, present address and at least one emergency contact.; The Unit and Job Role already exist in HRISense.; You do NOT need to prepare an employee number — HRISense generates it.
Step 1. Start the wizard: On the **Employees** page select **+ Add Employee**, or select **Add Employee** in the menu on the left. (Where: Employees page -> + Add Employee. Result: The wizard opens at Step 1, Personal Information, with all eight steps shown across the top.)
Step 2. Step 1 — Personal Information: Fill in **First Name**, **Middle Name** (if any), **Last Name**, **Sex**, **Date of Birth** and **Civil Status**. **Blood Type**, **Number of Children** and **Spouse Name** (shown when civil status is not Single) are optional. Then select **Next**. (Where: Onboarding wizard -> Step 1 -> Next. Tip: Spell names exactly as they appear on government IDs. Leave an optional field blank rather than typing "N/A" — blank means not provided, and 0 is a real answer for children.. Warning: If a required field is empty, HRISense tells you which one before letting you move on.. Result: The wizard moves to Step 2, Contact & Address.)
Step 3. Step 2 — Contact & Address: Fill in **Personal Email (login)**, **Mobile Number** and **Present Address**. Add a telephone number, **Permanent / Provincial Address**, and — only for staff who live at Hospicio — **HSJ Residence** and **Unit / Dorm**, then select **Next**. (Where: Onboarding wizard -> Step 2 -> Next. The personal email is the employee's HRISense sign-in email, and the welcome message with the temporary password is sent to it. There is no separate work email.. Warning: Personal email, mobile number and present address are required. The personal email cannot already be another account's login.. Result: The wizard moves to Step 3, Employment Details.)
Step 4. Step 3 — Employment Details: Choose the **Unit**, **Job Role**, **Work Schedule**, **Employment Status**, **Employment State** and **Date Hired**, then select **Next**. (Where: Onboarding wizard -> Step 3 -> Next. HRISense works out the immediate supervisor from the job role hierarchy and shows the result on this step (or why it is pending). To use someone else, select **Change Supervisor**, choose an active employee and give a reason — it is saved as a manual override. On this step you also tick **Leave eligibility** (Paternity, Solo Parent) if HR has confirmed it; HRISense never infers it.. Result: The wizard moves to Step 4, and the supervisor preview shows either a name or a pending notice.)
Step 5. Step 4 — Government Numbers: Enter the **SSS**, **PhilHealth**, **Pag-IBIG** and **TIN** numbers. For any other ID (passport, UMID …) select **+ Add Government ID** and fill in the **ID Type** and **ID Number**. Then select **Next**. (Where: Onboarding wizard -> Step 4 -> Next. Tip: Leave a box blank if the number has not been issued yet — you can add it later from the 201 profile.. Result: The wizard moves to Step 5, Emergency Contacts.)
Step 6. Step 5 — Emergency Contacts: Enter **Emergency Contact 1** — **Contact Person**, **Relationship** and **Mobile Number**. Select **+ Add Emergency Contact** for up to two more, then select **Next**. (Where: Onboarding wizard -> Step 5 -> Next. Warning: The first contact is required. Every contact you add needs all three details. At most three contacts.. Result: The wizard moves to Step 6, Education & Licenses.)
Step 7. Step 6 — Education & Licenses: Fill in what applies, then select **Next**: the **PRC License #** and **Profession** (then its **Issued** and **Valid Until** dates); a TESDA **national certificate** number, qualification and valid-until date; and **education** — schools, course, **Graduated**, diploma and vocational qualification. (Where: Onboarding wizard -> Step 6 -> Next. Tip: Everything on this step is optional. Leave PRC and NC blank for roles that do not need them — they never lower profile completion.. Result: The wizard moves to Step 7, Document Uploads.)
Step 8. Step 7 — Document Uploads: Attach the **Profile Photo**, **Resume / CV**, **Employment Contract**, **Government IDs** and any other documents (license, certificate and diploma copies included), then select **Next**. (Where: Onboarding wizard -> Step 7 -> Next. Tip: This step is optional. You can add documents at any time from the Documents tab of the 201 profile.. Result: The wizard moves to Step 8, Review & Confirm.)
Step 9. Step 8 — Review & Confirm: Check the summary, including the welcome-email preview showing the personal email address it will go to. Use **Back** to correct anything or **Save as Draft** to finish later. When everything is right, select **Confirm & Onboard Employee**. (Where: Onboarding wizard -> Step 8 -> Confirm & Onboard Employee. Warning: The temporary password appears only once, on the screen that follows. Copy it or download the PDF before you leave the page.. Result: A confirmation screen shows the generated employee number (HSJ-XXXX), the sign-in email, how many documents were saved, the one-time temporary password, and whether the welcome email actually reached the employee.)
What happens next: The employee appears in the directory and the org chart, and can sign in with the sign-in email and temporary password. They must set their own password the first time. If the confirmation screen said the welcome email was not delivered, give the temporary password to the employee yourself.
Problem: It says a HRISense account already exists for this email. — Solution: Each login email must be unique. Check whether the person already has a record, including an archived one, before creating a new account.
Problem: It lists fields I still need to complete. — Solution: Go back to the step named in the message. Personal email, mobile number, present address and emergency contact 1 (person, relationship and mobile number) are required.
Problem: I closed the page before saving the temporary password. — Solution: The password is never shown again. Open the 201 profile, go to Account Management, and use Reset & send new credentials.
Problem: The screen says the welcome email was not sent. — Solution: Email delivery may be switched off for this installation, or the address may be unreachable. Give the credentials to the employee directly and ask your system administrator to check the email settings.
Problem: The summary says supervisor assignment is pending. — Solution: The employee is still created. Open their 201 profile and use Override Supervisor, or ask for the job role hierarchy to be confirmed.
Tip: HRISense generates the employee number itself, in the format HSJ-XXXX. You never type it in.
Tip: Use Download PDF on the confirmation screen to save a credential sheet you can hand to the employee.

entries.title: How to Save, Resume and Discard Onboarding Drafts
entries.text:
Pick up an unfinished onboarding, or remove a draft for someone who did not report.
Purpose: Continue an onboarding you started earlier, or clear away one that is no longer needed.
When to use: When you were interrupted mid-onboarding, or when a candidate did not report for duty.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; At least one draft has been saved.
Step 1. Save your progress: At any step of the onboarding wizard, select **Save as Draft**. (Where: Onboarding wizard -> Save as Draft. Everything you have typed so far is kept, and the draft appears under Draft Employees.. Result: A confirmation appears and the sidebar badge next to Draft Employees increases.)
Step 2. Open the drafts list: In the menu on the left, open **Employees** and select **Draft Employees**. (Where: Left menu -> Employees -> Draft Employees. Result: The drafts page lists each saved onboarding with the name entered so far and when it was last changed.)
Step 3. Resume or discard: Select **Resume** to reopen the wizard with everything filled in as you left it. To remove a draft for someone who will not be joining, select the delete action and confirm. (Where: Draft Employees -> Resume / Delete. Warning: Deleting a draft permanently removes the information typed into it. It does not affect any real employee record.. Result: Resuming reopens the wizard; deleting removes the draft from the list.)
What happens next: When you finalise a resumed draft, the draft is closed automatically and the employee joins the active directory.
Problem: The drafts page is empty. — Solution: All previous drafts were either finalised or deleted. Select + Add Employee to start a new one.
Problem: A draft came from a hired applicant. — Solution: Applicants converted from Recruitment arrive here with their details already filled in. Resume the draft and complete the remaining steps as usual.
Tip: The number beside Draft Employees in the menu is how many drafts are waiting.

entries.title: How to Read an Employee 201 Profile
entries.text:
Move around the sections of a personnel file in Employee Management and understand what each one holds.
Purpose: Find any piece of information HRISense holds about one employee.
When to use: When you need somebody's contact details, schedule, documents, compliance standing or history.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel (HR Officer or Sister).; Employee Management is HR's screen. Supervisors see their direct reports in **My Team**; everyone sees themselves in **My Profile**.
Step 1. Open the profile: From the **Employees** directory, select the employee's row. (Where: Employees directory -> employee row. Result: The profile opens, labelled Employee Management, with the employee's photo, name, employee number, job role and status tags at the top, and a profile completion figure on the right.)
Step 2. Move between the sections: Use the section list: **Profile** (Overview, Personal, Contact, Employment, Government, Education, Emergency), **Work** (Schedule, Attendance, Leave Balances, Evaluations, Training), **Records** (Documents, Compliance, Medical, Psychological, Timeline) and **Access** (Account Management). (Where: Employee profile -> section list. Employment shows the employment status, employee status, date hired and length of service, the immediate supervisor and any additional overseers.. Where a value has not been filled in, the profile says "Not provided" rather than leaving the space blank or showing a placeholder.. Result: The chosen section loads beside the list (below it on a phone).)
Step 3. Use the profile completion figure: On the right of the header, check the completion percentage, select **View breakdown**, and use **View all** to see the missing items. (Where: Employee profile -> Profile completion. The breakdown names every part of the 201 file, its points, and whether it is complete, so you know exactly what to chase.. Result: You can see at a glance what is still outstanding for this employee.)
What happens next: From the profile you can edit details, manage documents, set the weekly schedule, override the supervisor, archive or restore, and manage the login account.
Problem: A section says there are no records. — Solution: That is normal for a new employee. Training, evaluation and attendance history only build up over time.
Problem: I opened my own record here. — Solution: That is your record as Employee Management shows it. For your self-service view, open **My Profile** in the menu on the left.
Tip: Use **Back to Employee Directory** at the top left to return to the employee list.

entries.title: How to Open Your Own Profile (My Profile)
entries.text:
Find your own records — personal and contact details, employment, schedule, attendance, leave, evaluations, training and compliance.
Purpose: See the information HRISense holds about you, in one place.
When to use: To check your details, schedule, attendance, leave balance, evaluations, training or compliance, or to see how complete your profile is.
Before you start: You are signed in to HRISense. Every account has My Profile — HR, Sister, supervisors, heads, coordinators and employees.
Step 1. Open My Profile: Select **My Profile** in the menu on the left (just under Dashboard). You can also select your name at the top right and choose **My Profile**. (Where: Left menu -> My Profile. Result: Your profile opens with your photo, name, job role, unit, employee ID, status and profile completion at the top.)
Step 2. Look through your sections: Use the section list: **My Profile** (Overview, Personal, Contact, Employment, Government, Education & Licenses, Emergency, Documents), **Work** (Schedule, Attendance, Leave, Evaluations, Training), **Health & Compliance** (Compliance, Medical, Psychological) and **Account** (Account & Security, Record History). (Where: My Profile -> section list. You see only your own records, and each area follows its own privacy rules — for example, documents appear only when HR has marked them visible to you, and medical and psychological records show what those modules show an employee.. Result: Each section shows your own information.)
Step 3. Check your profile completion: Select **View breakdown** under the percentage. (Where: My Profile -> Profile completion -> View breakdown. It lists every item that counts, its points, and whether it is complete or missing. Sections with missing items show a red count in the section list.. Result: You know exactly what is still missing.)
What happens next: To change your phone numbers, addresses, emergency contacts or religion, select **Edit My Profile**. Everything else is kept by HR.
Problem: My name, job role, unit or government numbers are wrong. — Solution: These are kept by HR. Ask HR Personnel to correct them.
Problem: A document I expected is not listed. — Solution: Only documents HR has marked as visible to the employee appear on your profile.
Tip: HR and Sister also use My Profile for themselves; administering employee records stays in Employee Management.

entries.title: How to Update Your Own Details (Edit My Profile)
entries.text:
Change your phone numbers, addresses, emergency contacts and religion yourself.
Purpose: Keep your own contact information up to date without waiting for HR.
When to use: When you move, change your phone number, or need to change who HR should call in an emergency.
Before you start: You are signed in to HRISense.
Step 1. Open Edit My Profile: Open **My Profile** and select **Edit My Profile** in the header. (Where: My Profile -> Edit My Profile. Result: A short form opens with only the details you can change: mobile number, home phone, present address, permanent address, religion and emergency contacts.)
Step 2. Make your changes: Change what you need. You can list up to three emergency contacts; the first one is required. Mobile number and present address cannot be left blank. (Where: Edit My Profile. Your name, personal email (which is also how you sign in), employment details, job role, unit, supervisor, government IDs and profile photo are kept by HR, so they are not in this form.. Result: The **Review changes** button becomes available once something has changed.)
Step 3. Review and save: Select **Review changes**, check the list of old and new values, then select **Save changes**. (Where: Edit My Profile -> Review changes -> Save changes. Result: "Your profile has been updated." Your profile shows the new details.)
What happens next: The change is recorded in your record's history. HR sees the updated details straight away.
Problem: I need to change my email address. — Solution: Your personal email is also your sign-in, so HR Personnel changes it for you.
Problem: I want to change my profile photo. — Solution: Profile photos are filed by HR at onboarding; HRISense has no self-service photo upload.
Tip: Select **Back to editing** on the review step to change something before you save.

entries.title: How to Use My Team
entries.text:
See the employees who report directly to you, and open a team member's work profile.
Purpose: Look after the employees you are responsible for: their schedules, attendance, leave, training, compliance and documents.
When to use: When you need to check on someone who reports to you.
Before you start: You are signed in as a supervisor, head or coordinator.; My Team lists the employees whose immediate supervisor is you. HR sets reporting lines.
Step 1. Open My Team: Select **My Team** in the menu on the left. (Where: Left menu -> My Team. Result: Your direct reports are listed with their job role, unit, status and profile completion. On a phone each person is a card.)
Step 2. Find someone: Search by name, employee ID or job role, or filter by job role or status. Select a completion percentage to see how it is calculated. (Where: My Team -> search and filters. Result: The list narrows to the people you are looking for.)
Step 3. Open a team member: Select **View** (or **View profile** on a phone). (Where: My Team -> View. The Team Member Profile shows their work profile and the sections a supervisor uses: Schedule (you can set their weekly schedule), Attendance, Leave Requests, Training, Compliance and Documents.. Result: The profile opens under *My Team → their name*.)
What happens next: To endorse a pending leave request, select **Open Leave Requests** from the Leave Requests section. Evaluations you are asked to give are under **Evaluations**.
Problem: Someone in my unit is not on My Team. — Solution: My Team follows reporting lines, not units. If they should report to you, ask HR to check their immediate supervisor.
Problem: I cannot see a team member's address, phone numbers or government IDs. — Solution: Personal details stay between HR and the employee. Supervisors see the work profile.
Problem: It says "This employee is not on your team". — Solution: You can open only the people who report directly to you — not a coordinator's staff below you, and not archived records.
Tip: Supervisors cannot edit, archive or restore employee records; those changes go through HR.

entries.title: How to Edit Employee Details
entries.text:
Correct personal, contact, employment or government information on a 201 file.
Purpose: Keep an employee's 201 file accurate when something changes.
When to use: On a change of address or phone number, a move to another unit, a change of job role, or a correction to government numbers.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; You have the correct new information, ideally with supporting documents.
Step 1. Open the edit form: Open the employee's 201 profile and select **Edit Profile** at the top right. (Where: Employee profile -> Edit Profile. Result: The edit form opens with the current values filled in.)
Step 2. Change what needs changing: Update the fields you need. Changing the **Unit** clears the Department and Job Role so you can pick ones that belong to the new unit. (Where: Edit form. Warning: Changing the job role can change what the employee is allowed to see in HRISense, because permissions follow the job role.. Result: The form shows your new values.)
Step 3. Save: Select **Review Changes**, check the list of old and new values, then select **Confirm Save**. (Where: Edit form -> Review Changes -> Confirm Save. The change is recorded in the employee's Timeline, showing who made it and when.. Result: A confirmation appears and the profile shows the updated values.)
What happens next: The updated values are used everywhere in HRISense straight away, and the change is visible in the Timeline tab.
Problem: The job role list is empty after I changed the unit. — Solution: Job roles belong to units. Choose the unit first, then the department, then the job role.
Problem: It says the email address is already in use. — Solution: The personal email is also the login, so it must be unique. Check whether another record — possibly an archived one — already uses it.
Tip: Use the Timeline tab to see the history of changes made to a record.

entries.title: How to Set or Override an Employee's Supervisor
entries.text:
Correct the reporting line when the automatic assignment is not right.
Purpose: Make sure each employee reports to the right person, because the reporting line decides who can see their records and endorse their leave.
When to use: When a profile shows "Pending HR Review" for the supervisor, or when the automatically chosen supervisor is not the right one.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; You know who the employee actually reports to.
Step 1. Open the Employment tab: Open the employee's 201 profile and select the **Employment** tab. (Where: Employee profile -> Employment. The Immediate Supervisor section shows the current supervisor, how it was decided, and any pending notice.. Result: You can see either a supervisor card or a note that no supervisor is assigned.)
Step 2. Choose Override Supervisor: Select **Override Supervisor**, choose the correct person from the list, and type the reason for the change. (Where: Employment tab -> Override Supervisor. Warning: A reason is required. It is stored with the record so anyone reviewing the file later can see why the reporting line was changed by hand.. Result: The dialog accepts your choice and the reason.)
Step 3. Save the assignment: Confirm the change. (Where: Override dialog -> confirm. Result: The Employment tab shows the new supervisor with a "Manual Override Active" note and your reason.)
What happens next: The new supervisor can see this employee in their team, view their attendance, and endorse their leave requests. The change is recorded in the Timeline.
Problem: The profile says "Pending HR Review". — Solution: HRISense could not work out a supervisor from the job role hierarchy. Set one by hand using Override Supervisor.
Problem: A supervisor says they cannot see one of their staff. — Solution: Open that employee's Employment tab and check who is recorded as their immediate supervisor.
Tip: The Org Chart is the quickest way to see whether reporting lines look right across a whole unit.

entries.title: How to Manage an Employee's Login Account
entries.text:
Activate, deactivate, lock, unlock or force a password change from the 201 profile.
Purpose: Control whether and how an employee can sign in to HRISense.
When to use: When somebody goes on extended leave, when an account needs to be locked for security, or when an employee is locked out.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; The employee has a login account.
Step 1. Open Account Management: Open the employee's 201 profile and select the **Account Management** tab. (Where: Employee profile -> Account Management. Result: The panel shows the sign-in email, when the account was created, when the employee last signed in, and whether the account is active or locked.)
Step 2. Activate or deactivate: Use **Deactivate** to stop the employee signing in without deleting anything, and **Activate** to restore access. (Where: Account Management -> Activate / Deactivate. A deactivated account keeps all its records. The employee simply cannot sign in.. Warning: You cannot deactivate or lock your own account; another HR administrator must.. Result: The status shown at the top of the panel changes.)
Step 3. Lock or unlock: Use **Lock** to block sign-in for one hour for a security concern, and **Unlock** to clear it. Wrong passwords never lock an account — they only make the browser that typed them wait. (Where: Account Management -> Lock / Unlock. Result: The lock state changes, and an unlocked account can sign in again straight away.)
Step 4. Force a password change: Under **Force password change**, select **Require change** to make the employee set a new password the next time they sign in. (Where: Account Management -> Force password change. Their current password keeps working until they sign in, at which point they must choose a new one. Use this when a password may have been seen by somebody else but the employee still knows it.. Result: The panel shows that a password change is required at the next sign-in.)
What happens next: Every one of these actions is recorded in the activity history with your name and the time.
Problem: The tab says the employee has no login account. — Solution: Accounts are created during onboarding. If an older record has none, contact your system administrator.
Problem: An employee says they are locked out but the panel shows no lock. — Solution: Wrong passwords make their browser wait (up to 15 minutes) without locking the account, so they can still sign in from another device, and Unlock does not shorten that wait. Also check whether the account is deactivated. Reset & send new credentials is the quickest fix for a forgotten password.
Tip: Deactivate is the right choice for long absences; lock is for security concerns.

entries.title: How to Issue New Credentials to an Employee
entries.text:
Give a new temporary password to someone who cannot sign in.
Purpose: Get an employee back into HRISense when they cannot sign in and cannot use the self-service reset.
When to use: When an employee lost their welcome email, forgot their password and cannot receive email, or their temporary password expired unused.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; The employee has a login account.
Step 1. Open Account Management: Open the employee's 201 profile and select the **Account Management** tab. (Where: Employee profile -> Account Management. Result: The account panel opens.)
Step 2. Choose Reset & send new credentials: Under **Reset & send new credentials**, select **Reset**, then **Reset & send** to confirm. (Where: Account Management -> Reset & send new credentials. HRISense never stores passwords in readable form, so an old password can never be looked up or re-sent. A reset always creates a brand-new temporary password.. Warning: The employee's current password stops working immediately and all their open sessions are signed out.. Result: A new temporary password is shown on screen once, together with a message saying whether the email reached the employee.)
Step 3. Pass the password on if the email did not go: If the message says the email was not delivered, copy the temporary password and give it to the employee directly. (Where: Account Management -> temporary password panel. Warning: Never send a password over an unsecured group chat, and never leave it written at a shared workstation.. Result: The employee has a working temporary password.)
What happens next: The employee signs in with the temporary password and is required to set their own password immediately.
Problem: The message says the email could not be delivered. — Solution: Give the password to the employee directly. Ask your system administrator to check the email settings if this keeps happening.
Problem: The employee would rather reset it themselves. — Solution: They can use "Forgot password?" on the sign-in page, as long as they can open the mailbox their account uses.
Tip: The message is sent to the employee's personal email address, the same address they sign in with.

entries.title: How to Upload a Document to a 201 File
entries.text:
Attach a contract, clearance, certificate or ID to an employee record.
Purpose: Keep an employee's supporting documents in their 201 file rather than in a separate folder.
When to use: When a new contract is signed, a clearance is renewed, or a certificate is issued.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; The file is a PDF, JPG, PNG, WEBP, DOC or DOCX and is no larger than the size limit shown in the dialog.
Step 1. Open the Documents tab: Open the employee's 201 profile and select the **Documents** tab, then select **Upload File**. (Where: Employee profile -> Documents -> Upload File. Result: The upload dialog opens.)
Step 2. Choose the file and its category: Select the file, then choose the **Category** that fits it — Resume, Employment Contract, Government ID, Medical Clearance, Certificate or Other. Add a note if it helps. (Where: Upload dialog. The category is what the Documents tab groups by, so choosing it correctly makes the file easy to find later.. Result: The dialog shows the file name and size and your chosen category.)
Step 3. Set who may see it, then upload: Decide whether the document should be visible to the employee and to their supervisor, then select **Upload**. (Where: Upload dialog -> Upload. Warning: Medical clearances and confidential documents should not be made visible to supervisors.. Result: The document appears in the Documents tab with its category, file type, size and upload date.)
What happens next: The document counts towards the employee's profile completion, and the upload is recorded in the activity history.
Problem: It refuses the file type. — Solution: Only PDF, JPG, PNG, WEBP, DOC and DOCX files are accepted. Programs and scripts are always rejected.
Problem: The file is too large. — Solution: Scan at a lower resolution or save the PDF at a smaller size, then upload again.
Tip: Give scanned files meaningful names before uploading — the original file name is what everyone sees in the list.

entries.title: How to Preview and Download 201 Documents
entries.text:
Open or save a document stored on an employee record.
Purpose: Read or save a document that is stored against an employee record.
When to use: When you need a copy of a contract, clearance or certificate.
Before you start: You are signed in.; The document is one you are allowed to see. Employees see documents marked visible to the employee; supervisors see documents marked visible to supervisors for their direct reports; HR Personnel see everything.
Step 1. Open the Documents tab: Open the 201 profile and select the **Documents** tab. (Where: Employee profile -> Documents. Result: Each document is shown as a card with its name, category, file type, size and upload date.)
Step 2. Preview or download: Select **Preview** to open a PDF or image in a new tab, or **Download** to save the file with its original name. (Where: Documents tab -> Preview / Download. Documents are never left open on the internet. HRISense checks who you are each time you open one, which is why they cannot be opened by copying a link.. Result: The document opens in a new tab, or your browser saves it.)
What happens next: Nothing is changed on the record — previewing and downloading are read-only actions.
Problem: Nothing opens when I select Preview. — Solution: Your browser may be blocking pop-ups. Allow pop-ups for HRISense, or use Download instead.
Problem: Preview is not offered for a document. — Solution: Only PDFs and images can be previewed in the browser. Word documents must be downloaded.
Problem: A document I expected is not in the list. — Solution: You only see documents you are allowed to see. Ask HR Personnel if you believe something is missing.
Tip: Downloaded files keep their original name, so they are easy to recognise afterwards.

entries.title: How to Edit, Replace or Remove a 201 Document
entries.text:
Correct a document's details, swap in a newer copy, or take one out of the file.
Purpose: Keep the documents in a 201 file correct and current.
When to use: When a document was filed under the wrong category, when a newer version is issued, or when something was uploaded to the wrong record.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.
Step 1. Edit the details: On the **Documents** tab, select **Edit** on the document card to change its category, note, or who may see it. (Where: Documents tab -> Edit. Result: The card shows the new category and visibility tags.)
Step 2. Replace the file: Select **Replace** to upload a newer copy in place of the existing one, keeping the same category and notes. (Where: Documents tab -> Replace. Use this for a renewed clearance or a re-signed contract, so the file history stays in one place.. Result: The card shows the new file name, size and date.)
Step 3. Remove a document: Select **Delete** and confirm. (Where: Documents tab -> Delete. Warning: Only remove a document that should never have been filed here, for example one uploaded to the wrong employee. Superseded documents are better replaced than deleted, so the record keeps its history.. Result: The document no longer appears in the Documents tab.)
What happens next: Every change is recorded in the activity history with your name and the time.
Problem: I deleted the wrong document. — Solution: Upload it again from your own copy. Contact your system administrator if you no longer have one.
Tip: Replace keeps the document's place in the file; delete removes it entirely.

entries.title: How to Archive and Restore an Employee Record
entries.text:
Move a separated employee out of the active directory, and bring one back on rehire.
Purpose: Take a separated employee out of day-to-day lists while keeping their complete history.
When to use: When an employee resigns, retires or ends their contract — and again if they are rehired.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.
Step 1. Archive the record: Open the employee's 201 profile and select **Archive**. Type the reason when asked, then confirm. (Where: Employee profile -> Archive. Warning: Archiving disables the login account and removes the employee from active directory lists. Nothing is deleted — all 201 records, documents and history are kept.. Result: The profile shows an ARCHIVED banner and the employee no longer appears in the active directory.)
Step 2. Find an archived employee: In the menu on the left, open **Employees** and select **Archived Employees**. (Where: Left menu -> Employees -> Archived Employees. Result: The archived list opens.)
Step 3. Restore on rehire: Select **Restore** on the record. Choose whether to restore their login access at the same time. (Where: Archived Employees -> Restore. Restoring the record and restoring sign-in access are separate decisions, so you can bring a record back without re-enabling the account until you are ready.. Result: The employee is back in the active directory, with all previous documents and history intact.)
What happens next: Archived records remain available for auditing. Restored employees appear in the directory and the org chart again.
Problem: A restored employee cannot sign in. — Solution: Their account access was probably not restored at the same time. Open Account Management and activate the account, then issue new credentials if needed.
Problem: The Archive button is greyed out on my own record. — Solution: You cannot archive your own record — it would switch off your own sign-in. Another HR administrator or Sister must do it.
Problem: I cannot find a former employee anywhere. — Solution: Look under Archived Employees. Records are never deleted when somebody leaves.
Tip: Always archive rather than delete — the record is needed for audits and for any future rehire.

entries.title: How to Read the Organizational Chart
entries.text:
See the reporting structure of a unit and find who reports to whom.
Purpose: See how a unit is organised and who each person reports to.
When to use: When you need to know the reporting line for a leave endorsement, or you are checking that a unit's structure is set up correctly.
Before you start: You are signed in to HRISense.
Step 1. Open the org chart: HR: in the menu, open **Employees** and select **Org Chart**. Everyone else: type **Org Chart** in the search box at the top of the screen and select it. (Where: Left menu -> Employees -> Org Chart. What the chart shows depends on your access: HR sees everyone; a supervisor sees themselves and their direct reports; an employee sees themselves, the supervisors above them and anyone reporting to them.. Result: The chart opens showing the structure as a tree of cards.)
Step 2. Choose a unit and move around: Pick a unit to focus on, then expand or collapse a card to show or hide the staff who report to that person. Drag to move around and use the zoom controls to fit more on screen. (Where: Org Chart -> unit selector and node cards. Result: The chart redraws showing the branch you opened.)
Step 3. Read the status labels: Each card shows the person's name, employee number and job role, plus a label such as **Assigned**, **Manual Override** or a note that no supervisor is confirmed yet. (Where: Org Chart -> node card labels. A card showing that no supervisor is confirmed usually means the job role hierarchy still needs to be set up, or the person is at the top of that branch.. Result: You can tell which reporting lines are confirmed and which still need attention.)
Step 4. See additional oversight (optional): Switch **Show Additional Oversight** to **ON**. Dashed teal lines then run from a person to the people they **also** oversee in other branches (solid grey lines are still the normal reporting lines), cards show **Additional Oversight: n** — open it to see the **Immediate supervisor**, **Also overseen by** and **Also oversees** — and a list groups every relationship by overseer. Switch it **OFF** to return to the normal chart. (Where: Org Chart -> Show Additional Oversight. Additional oversight never moves anyone: each person stays in their own branch with their immediate supervisor unchanged, and it gives no extra access to leave, evaluations, attendance or anything else. HR Personnel manage it with **Manage Additional Oversight**, choosing the actual person and who they oversee — one employee, or everyone in a job role.. Tip: On a phone the lines are hidden; read the cards and the Additional Oversight list instead.. Result: You can see who also oversees whom, apart from the normal reporting lines.)
What happens next: HR Personnel can correct any reporting line from the employee's Employment tab, and manage additional oversight with **Manage Additional Oversight** on the Org Chart or from the employee's profile.
Problem: Somebody is missing from the chart. — Solution: They may be archived, or in a different unit from the one you are viewing. Check the unit selector first.
Problem: A branch shows a cycle warning. — Solution: Two people have been set as each other's supervisor. Ask HR Personnel to correct one of the two records.
Tip: Use the search box to jump straight to a person rather than hunting through branches.

entries.title: How to Add an Additional Overseer (Sub-Supervisor)
entries.text:
Record that someone also oversees an employee outside their normal reporting line, without changing the immediate supervisor.
Purpose: Show that a person — for example a specific Sister — also oversees an employee who sits in another branch.
When to use: When Hospicio has confirmed an extra oversight relationship on top of the normal reporting line.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; You know the exact person who oversees, not just their job title.
Step 1. Open the Employment section: Open the employee's profile in Employee Management and select **Employment**. Find **Additional Overseers (Sub-Supervisors)**. (Where: Employee profile -> Employment -> Additional Overseers. It shows the **Immediate supervisor (primary)**, any **Additional overseer**, and whom this employee also oversees.. Result: You see the current relationships.)
Step 2. Choose the overseer: Select **Add additional overseer** and choose the actual person. (Where: Additional Overseers -> Add additional overseer. Result: The person is selected.)
Step 3. Decide about their team: If this employee handles other staff, choose **No — only this employee**, or **Yes** and tick which of the employees they handle to include. Check the **Preview** tree. (Where: Add additional overseer -> include their team -> Preview. Result: The preview shows exactly who will be covered.)
Step 4. Confirm: Select **Confirm**. To remove a relationship later, use **Remove** beside it. (Where: Add additional overseer -> Confirm. Result: The overseer appears on the profile and as a dashed line on the Org Chart when **Show Additional Oversight** is on.)
What happens next: Nothing else changes: the employee keeps their immediate supervisor, branch, unit and job role.
Problem: Will the overseer now approve this employee's leave or evaluations? — Solution: No. Additional oversight is shown on the profile and Org Chart only. Leave endorsement, evaluations, attendance and all other access still follow the immediate supervisor.
Problem: Someone is reported as already covered. — Solution: They already have this relationship, or already report directly to the overseer, so nothing new is added for them.
Tip: To cover everyone who holds a job role, now and later, use **Manage Additional Oversight** on the Org Chart instead.

entries.title: How to Create a Job Opening
entries.text:
Draft a vacancy with its unit, job role, description and closing date.
Purpose: Record a vacancy in HRISense so applications can be collected against it.
When to use: When a unit has an approved vacancy to fill.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; The Unit and Job Role for the position already exist in HRISense.
Step 1. Start a new opening: In the menu on the left, open **Recruitment** and select **Job Openings**, then select **New Opening**. (Where: Left menu -> Recruitment -> Job Openings -> New Opening. Result: The Create Job Opening form opens.)
Step 2. Choose the position: Under **Position**, select the **Job Role / Position** from Hospicio's current job roles (grouped by unit). Its unit and department fill in, and the **Posting title** starts as the position's title — adjust it only if the posting needs more detail. If the position does not exist yet, select **New position**: give its title, unit, optional department, the position it reports to, and whether it is staff or supervisory. A title that matches an existing role is offered instead, so no duplicate is created. Then fill in **Vacancy** (employment type, vacancies, opening and closing dates). (Where: Create Job Opening -> Position / Vacancy. Using the real job role means a hired applicant can be converted straight into an onboarding draft with the right placement already filled in. The **Careers preview** on the right shows how the posting will look.. Result: The position, unit and vacancy details are complete.)
Step 3. Add dates and the description: Set the **Opening Date** and **Closing Date**, then write the **Description**, **Responsibilities** and **Qualifications**. List any documents applicants must attach. (Where: Create Job Opening -> Description and qualifications. Tip: The closing date must be on or after the opening date. Clear qualifications reduce the number of unsuitable applications.. Result: The posting content is complete.)
Step 4. Save: Select **Save as Draft** to keep it private for now, or **Save & Publish** to put it on the public Careers page straight away. (Where: Create Job Opening -> Save as Draft / Save & Publish. Result: A confirmation appears and the job opening detail page opens with its status tag.)
What happens next: A published opening appears on the public Careers page and can receive applications. A draft stays private until you publish it.
Problem: It says required fields are missing. — Solution: The position, posting title, unit, description, responsibilities and qualifications must all be filled in.
Problem: The job role list is empty. — Solution: Job roles belong to units. Choose the unit first.
Tip: You can edit any of this later from the job opening detail page.

entries.title: How to Publish, Close, Fill or Archive a Job Opening
entries.text:
Control whether a vacancy is on the public Careers page and when it stops accepting applications.
Purpose: Move a vacancy through its life: Draft → Open → Closed or Filled → Archived.
When to use: When a vacancy is ready to advertise, stops taking applications, is filled, or is no longer needed day to day.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel. Publishing is the HR Officer's or a Sister's decision; HRISense refuses it for other HR staff.; The job opening exists.
Step 1. Open the job opening: In the menu, open **Recruitment** → **Job Openings** and select the opening. (Where: Recruitment -> Job Openings -> opening. Result: The opening shows its status, details and timeline.)
Step 2. Publish a draft: On a **Draft**, select **Publish** and confirm. (Where: Job opening -> Publish. An open opening appears on the public Careers page only while today falls between its opening and closing dates.. Result: The status becomes Open.)
Step 3. Close or mark it filled: On an **Open** opening, select **Close** to stop new applications, or **Mark Filled** when the post has been filled. (Where: Job opening -> Close / Mark Filled. Result: The opening leaves the Careers page. Applications already received are kept.)
Step 4. Archive: On a **Closed** or **Filled** opening, select **Archive** when it no longer needs to appear in active lists. (Where: Job opening -> Archive. Result: The opening is hidden from normal lists; its history stays.)
What happens next: Applicants already in progress are not affected — continue with them from **Applicants**.
Problem: The opening is Open but not on the Careers page. — Solution: Check its opening and closing dates: it shows only while today is inside them.
Problem: Publishing is refused. — Solution: Only the HR Officer or a Sister can publish. Ask one of them to publish the opening.
Tip: Close rather than archive while you might still need the opening in your active lists.

entries.title: How to Review Applicants and Change Their Status
entries.text:
Find an application, keep internal notes, and move the applicant through the stages.
Purpose: Work through the applications for a vacancy and record where each candidate stands.
When to use: Whenever applications need reviewing or a candidate moves to the next stage.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; The final hire or reject decision belongs to the HR Officer or a Sister.
Step 1. Find the application: In the menu, open **Recruitment** → **Applicants**. Use the search and filters, then select **View** on the application. (Where: Recruitment -> Applicants -> View. Result: The application opens with Position Details, Personal Information, Internal Notes and Status History.)
Step 2. Keep internal notes: Add your observations under **Internal Notes**. (Where: Applicant -> Internal Notes. Notes are private to HR. Applicants never see them.. Result: The note is saved on the application.)
Step 3. Change the status: Select **Update Status**, choose the new status — **Under Review**, **For Interview**, **For Requirements**, **Hired**, **Rejected** or **Withdrawn** — add an internal reason if needed, and select **Confirm Status Change**. (Where: Applicant -> Update Status -> Confirm Status Change. Warning: Each status change sends the matching automatic email to the applicant (for example *Application under review* or *Application not selected*). **Hired** is final and cannot be undone.. Result: The status changes and appears in the Status History.)
Step 4. Check the email: Open **Email Communications** to see the email that went out and its result. (Where: Applicant -> Email Communications. Result: The email is listed as Sent, Simulated (email sending is switched off) or Failed.)
What happens next: A **Hired** applicant can be turned into an onboarding draft from **Hiring & Onboarding**.
Problem: I cannot find an applicant. — Solution: Clear the search and filters, or search by the reference number the applicant quotes.
Problem: I marked someone Hired by mistake. — Solution: Hired cannot be reverted. If an onboarding draft was created, delete that draft instead.
Tip: The reference number is the quickest way to find an application an applicant asks about.

entries.title: How to Review an Applicant's Documents
entries.text:
Open the résumé and cover letter an applicant submitted.
Purpose: Read the documents an applicant attached to their application.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; The applicant attached at least one document.
Step 1. Open the Documents tab: Open the application and select the **Documents** tab. (Where: Applicant -> Documents. Result: The submitted files are listed.)
Step 2. Preview or download: Select **Preview** to read a file in HRISense, or **Download File Securely** to save a copy. (Where: Documents -> Preview / Download File Securely. Warning: Applicant documents hold personal information. Opening one is recorded in the audit log — do not share them outside the hiring process.. Result: The document opens or downloads.)
What happens next: If the applicant is hired, file the documents that belong in their 201 file during onboarding.
Problem: A required document is missing. — Solution: Move the applicant to **For Requirements** (this sends the *Additional requirements* email), or write to them with **Compose Email**.
Tip: Applicants never get an HRISense account, so anything else you need is requested by email.

entries.title: How to Schedule and Update an Interview
entries.text:
Book an interview, reschedule or cancel it, and record how it went.
Purpose: Keep interview arrangements and results on the application itself.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; You know the date, time and interviewer.
Step 1. Schedule the interview: On the application, select **Schedule Interview**.
