Enter the **Date**, **Time**, **Interview Type** (Initial, Technical, Panel, Final or Other), **Interviewer** and **Location or Meeting Link**, then save. (Where: Applicant -> Interviews -> Schedule Interview. HRISense sends the applicant an interview invitation email automatically.. Result: The interview is listed as Scheduled.)
Step 2. Reschedule or cancel: Select **Edit** on the interview to change the date or time, or set its status to Cancelled. (Where: Interviews -> Edit. The applicant is emailed about the reschedule or cancellation automatically.. Result: The interview shows its new details or status.)
Step 3. Record the outcome: After the interview, select **Edit**, set the status to **Completed** or **No show**, and fill in the **Recommendation** and **Internal Notes**. (Where: Interviews -> Edit -> Status / Recommendation. Result: The result is kept on the application.)
What happens next: When interviews are done, change the applicant's status — for example to For Requirements, Hired or Rejected.
Problem: The applicant did not come. — Solution: Set the interview to **No show** and add a note. Keep the record — the history matters.
Tip: Interviews also appear on HR's dashboard calendar.

entries.title: Applicant Emails: Automatic Messages, Composing and Retrying
entries.text:
Which emails HRISense sends applicants by itself, how to write your own, and how to retry a failed one.
Purpose: Keep applicants informed and keep a record of every email they were sent.
When to use: When you need to write to an applicant, or an email failed.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; The applicant gave a valid email address.
Step 1. Know what is sent automatically: HRISense emails the applicant by itself when the application is received, when you change its status (Under Review, For Interview, For Requirements, Hired, Rejected, Withdrawn), and when an interview is scheduled, rescheduled or cancelled. (Where: Applicant -> Email Communications. If email sending is switched off on this server, each email is recorded as **Simulated** and nothing is sent.. Result: You know which messages you do not need to write yourself.)
Step 2. Write your own email: Select **Compose Email**, write the message, select **Preview & Send**, check it, then **Confirm Send**. (Where: Applicant -> Compose Email -> Preview & Send. Result: The email is listed under **Email Communications** with its result.)
Step 3. Retry a failed email: In **Email Communications**, select **Retry** on an email marked **Failed** and confirm. (Where: Email Communications -> Retry. Result: A new attempt is recorded with its result.)
What happens next: Every email stays on the application as a record of what the applicant was told.
Problem: A notification says an applicant email could not be sent. — Solution: Open that application's **Email Communications**, check the address, and select **Retry**.
Tip: Only failed emails can be retried.

entries.title: How to Turn a Hired Applicant into an Employee
entries.text:
Carry an applicant's details across into an onboarding draft.
Purpose: Avoid retyping an applicant's details when they join the hospital.
When to use: Once the hiring decision is made and the applicant has accepted.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; The applicant has been marked as hired.
Step 1. Mark the applicant as hired: On the applicant page, set the stage to **Hired**. (Where: Applicant page -> status -> Hired. Result: The conversion action becomes available.)
Step 2. Convert to an onboarding draft: In **Hiring & Onboarding**, select **Convert to Onboarding**. (Where: Applicant page -> Convert to Onboarding. The applicant's name, contact details and the position they applied for are copied into a new onboarding draft.. Result: A confirmation appears with a link to open the new draft.)
Step 3. Finish the onboarding: Open the draft from **Employees** -> **Draft Employees**, complete the remaining steps, and finalise. (Where: Employees -> Draft Employees -> Resume. Result: The employee is created, and the application is linked to the new employee record.)
What happens next: The application and the employee record stay linked, so the hiring history remains traceable from the 201 file.
Problem: Convert to Onboarding is not offered. — Solution: The applicant must be marked as hired first.
Problem: The draft is missing some details. — Solution: Only what the applicant supplied can be carried across. Fill in the rest during onboarding.
Tip: Check the personal email carried into the draft — that is where the welcome credentials will be sent.

entries.title: How the Public Careers Page Works
entries.text:
What applicants see: only the positions open right now.
Purpose: Understand what a member of the public sees, so you can guide an applicant over the phone.
When to use: When an applicant asks where to find your vacancies or how to apply.
Before you start: None. When nothing is open the page says so.
Step 1. Open the Careers page: Go to the HRISense address followed by **/careers**. No sign-in is needed. (Where: Browser -> /careers. Result: The page lists only the openings accepting applications now, with an **Open now** count. Search and the unit / employment-type filters narrow that list. With nothing open it says *There are no open positions right now*.)
Step 2. Open a vacancy: On an opening, select **View Opening** to read the full description, responsibilities, qualifications and the documents required. (Where: Careers -> vacancy. Result: The vacancy page opens with everything HR entered when creating the opening.)
Step 3. Start an application: Select **Apply Now** — on the opening card or on the vacancy page. (Where: Vacancy page -> Apply. Result: The application form opens.)
What happens next: Applications submitted here appear on the Applicants page inside HRISense.
Problem: An applicant cannot find a position on the Careers page. — Solution: Only an opening that is published (OPEN) and inside its opening and closing dates is listed. Check whether it is still a draft, has been closed or filled, or has passed its closing date.
Tip: Applicants never get an HRISense account. Everything they need is on the public pages.

entries.title: How an Applicant Submits an Application
entries.text:
The public application form and what happens after it is submitted.
Purpose: Apply for a published vacancy without needing an account.
When to use: When applying for a position at Hospicio de San Jose.
Before you start: The vacancy is published and still open.; You have your resume and any documents the vacancy asks for saved on your device.
Step 1. Open the application form: On the vacancy page, select the apply action. (Where: /careers -> vacancy -> Apply. Result: The application form opens.)
Step 2. Fill in your details: Enter your name, email address, mobile number (digits only, like 09171234567) and present address. **Sex** and **Religion** are optional — you may choose not to say. Tick **Privacy Consent** before submitting. (Where: Application form. Warning: Use an email address you check regularly. It is the only way the hospital can contact you about your application.. Result: The form is complete.)
Step 3. Attach your documents: Attach your resume and any documents listed on the vacancy. (Where: Application form -> attachments. Result: Each attached file is listed on the form.)
Step 4. Submit and keep your reference number: Tick **I'm not a robot** if it is shown, submit the application, then write down the reference number shown on the confirmation page. (Where: Application form -> submit. Warning: Keep the reference number and the status link. They are how you check your application later.. Result: A confirmation page shows your reference number, and an acknowledgement is emailed to you.)
What happens next: HR reviews the application. You will be contacted by email as it progresses, and you can check the status yourself using the link on your confirmation.
Problem: The file will not attach. — Solution: The résumé and cover letter must be PDF, DOC or DOCX, at most 5 MB each. The message under the file says which rule it broke.
Problem: The form says "Application already submitted". — Solution: An application for this same opening already uses your email address or mobile number. Use the status link in your confirmation email instead of applying again. You may still apply for a different opening.
Problem: The form says the request took too long, or that it could not connect. — Solution: Everything you entered is still on the form. Check your email first — if a confirmation arrived, the application was received. Otherwise select Submit Application again.
Problem: No acknowledgement email arrived. — Solution: Check your junk folder. Your application is still recorded — keep the reference number from the confirmation page.
Tip: Applying does not create an account. You do not need a password at any point.

entries.title: How to Check an Application Status Without Signing In
entries.text:
Use the secure status link to see how an application is progressing.
Purpose: Let an applicant see where their application stands without giving them an account.
When to use: Any time after submitting an application.
Before you start: You have the status link from your application confirmation or acknowledgement email.
Step 1. Open the status link: Open the status link from your confirmation page or acknowledgement email. (Where: Browser -> application status link. The link is unique to one application and cannot be guessed. It is read-only — nothing can be changed through it.. Result: The status page opens showing the position applied for and the current stage.)
Step 2. Read the status: Check the stage shown and any dates listed. (Where: Application status page. Only the information the hospital chooses to share is shown here. Internal notes and interview scores are never displayed.. Result: You can see the current stage of your application.)
What happens next: The page reflects the stage recorded in HRISense, so it updates as HR moves the application along.
Problem: The page says "This status link is not valid". — Solution: Copy the whole address, including everything after the last slash. If it still fails, contact HR with your reference number.
Problem: The page says "We couldn’t check your application". — Solution: The link is fine — the page could not reach HRISense. Select Try Again, or come back in a few minutes.
Problem: I lost the link. — Solution: Contact HR with your reference number and the email address you applied with.
Tip: Do not share the link — it is specific to one application.

entries.title: How to Monitor Daily Attendance
entries.text:
See the attendance recorded for any day — for the whole hospital (HR) or your own team (supervisors).
Purpose: Check the attendance recorded for a chosen day.
When to use: When you need to know who has an attendance record on a date, or to look at one person's punches.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel or as a Head, Supervisor or Coordinator.; Attendance for the period has been imported from the biometric export.
Step 1. Open Daily Monitoring: In the menu, open **Attendance** and select **Daily Monitoring**. (Where: Left menu -> Attendance -> Daily Monitoring. HR sees the **Calendar** and **Import** tabs for the whole hospital. Supervisors see **My Attendance** and **Team Attendance** (their direct reports only).. Result: A month calendar opens with summary cards for today.)
Step 2. Narrow it down (HR): Use the filters — unit, department, employee, work schedule, imported or not, and status. **Clear** resets them. (Where: Daily Monitoring -> filters. Result: The calendar counts only the people you chose.)
Step 3. Open a day: Select a date. A side panel lists each person with their status, their schedule that day, time in and time out, every recorded punch pair, the device's worked / overtime / undertime hours, and any review flags. (Where: Calendar -> date. Result: You see exactly what was recorded for that day.)
Step 4. Read the statuses carefully: Statuses are Present, Late, Absent, Half Day, On Leave, Holiday, Rest Day, Suspended, and **No imported record**. (Where: Day panel -> status. Warning: **No imported record** means no attendance data was received for that person and day. It is never treated as an absence.. Result: You know what HRISense actually holds for that day.)
What happens next: For totals over a period, use **Attendance Tally**.
Problem: Everyone shows "No imported record" for a date. — Solution: No attendance has been imported for that date yet. It is a data question, not an attendance problem.
Problem: A punch pair says "not closed". — Solution: The device recorded a clock-in without a matching clock-out. HR reviews it when importing.
Tip: A rest day comes from the weekly schedule; leave is a filed request; a holiday comes from the Holiday Calendar. They are recorded separately.

entries.title: How to Read the Attendance Tally
entries.text:
Attendance totals per person for a chosen period — yours, your team's, or everyone's.
Purpose: Get attendance totals for a period instead of looking one day at a time.
Before you start: You are signed in. HR sees everyone; a supervisor sees their team; an employee sees themselves.; Attendance for the period has been imported.
Step 1. Open the tally and choose a period: In the menu, open **Attendance** and select **Attendance Tally**. Choose **Today**, **This Week**, **This Month**, **Previous Month** or a custom range (up to 6 months). (Where: Left menu -> Attendance -> Attendance Tally. Result: The table shows totals for that period.)
Step 2. Read the counts: Each row counts the days recorded as Present, Late, Absent, Half Day and On Leave, the days with an imported record, and the days with no record. (Where: Attendance Tally -> table. Days with no record are days where nothing was received. They are not absences.. Result: You can compare people over the same period.)
What happens next: Use **Export** to save the tally as Excel, PDF or CSV.
Problem: The no-record count is high for everyone. — Solution: Part of the period has not been imported yet. Check the period covered before using the figures.
Tip: HRISense records attendance only. It does not calculate pay.

entries.title: How to Export an Attendance Tally
entries.text:
Save the tally as Excel, PDF or CSV.
Purpose: Take attendance totals out of HRISense for a meeting or a file copy.
When to use: When somebody needs the figures outside the system.
Before you start: You are signed in. The export holds what your tally shows: everyone for HR, your team for a supervisor, yourself for an employee.; The tally already shows the period (and, for HR, the filters) you want.
Step 1. Set the period and filters first: Choose the period — and, for HR, any unit or department filter — before exporting. (Where: Attendance Tally -> period and filters. The export contains exactly what the table shows, so getting the filters right first saves repeating the export.. Result: The table shows the rows you want to export.)
Step 2. Export: Select **Export** and choose Excel, PDF or CSV. (Where: Attendance Tally -> Export. Warning: The exported file contains employee information. Store it securely and do not email it outside the hospital.. Result: Your browser saves the file.)
What happens next: The file is a snapshot. Export again after any correction to attendance data.
Problem: Nothing downloads. — Solution: Your browser may be blocking the download. Allow downloads for HRISense and try again.
Tip: CSV is the easiest format to open in a spreadsheet for further sorting.

entries.title: How to Check Your Own Attendance
entries.text:
See the attendance recorded for you, and what each status means.
Purpose: Check the attendance HRISense holds for you.
Before you start: You are signed in to HRISense.
Step 1. Open your attendance: In the menu, open **Attendance** and select **Daily Monitoring**. Employees see their own **My Attendance** page; supervisors use the **My Attendance** tab. You can also open **My Profile** → **Attendance**. (Where: Attendance -> Daily Monitoring / My Profile -> Attendance. Result: A calendar of your recorded days opens.)
Step 2. Read a day: Select a date to see your status, schedule, time in and time out, and recorded punches. (Where: Calendar -> date. **No imported record** means nothing was received for that date. It is not a mark against you.. Result: You see what was recorded for that day.)
What happens next: If something looks wrong, tell your supervisor or HR with the date. Attendance comes from the biometric device and is checked by HR.
Problem: A day I worked shows no record. — Solution: Tell your supervisor or HR the date so they can check whether the device export for that day was imported.
Tip: **My Profile** → **Schedule** shows which days you are expected to work.

entries.title: How to Manage the Shift Catalog
entries.text:
Create and maintain the shifts that can be assigned to employees.
Purpose: Keep one shared list of shifts, so every weekly schedule uses the same definitions.
When to use: When a new shift pattern is introduced, or an existing one changes hours.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.
Step 1. Open the Shift Catalog: In the menu on the left, open **Attendance** and select **Work Schedule**, then open the **Shift Catalog** tab. (Where: Attendance -> Work Schedule -> Shift Catalog. Result: Every shift is listed with its category and its hours in 12-hour format.)
Step 2. Create a shift: Select **Create Shift**. Enter the **Shift Name**, choose the **Category** (Office or Shift), and set the **Start Time** and **End Time**. Add a description if it helps. (Where: Shift Catalog -> Create Shift. Tip: Name shifts the way staff describe them, for example "Morning Shift 8-5", so they are easy to pick correctly.. Result: The dialog holds your new shift details.)
Step 3. Save, edit or deactivate: Save the shift. Use the edit action to change an existing one, or deactivate a shift that is no longer used. (Where: Shift Catalog -> Save / Edit / Deactivate. Warning: Deactivating a shift stops it appearing in new schedules. Schedules already using it are not changed.. Result: The catalog shows your change, and the shift becomes available when setting weekly schedules.)
What happens next: The shift can now be chosen when configuring an employee's weekly schedule.
Problem: I cannot see the Shift Catalog tab. — Solution: It is available to HR Personnel only.
Problem: A shift crosses midnight. — Solution: Set the end time earlier than the start time. HRISense shows it as ending the next day.
Tip: Deactivate rather than delete, so historical schedules still make sense.

entries.title: How to Set an Employee's Weekly Schedule
entries.text:
Choose the regular shift, the rest days, and any day that differs.
Purpose: Record which days an employee works, which shift they work, and which days are their rest days.
When to use: When a new employee joins, when someone moves to a different pattern, or when rest days change.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel or a Supervisor.; The shifts you need already exist in the Shift Catalog.
Step 1. Open the schedule editor: Open the employee's profile (HR: Employee Management; supervisors: **My Team**), select the **Schedule** tab, and select **Set Weekly Schedule** or **Edit Schedule**. (Where: Employee profile -> Schedule -> Configure Weekly Schedule. Supervisors can set schedules for their direct reports only — not their own, which HR sets.. Result: The **Configure Weekly Schedule** window opens, showing the employee's name and the date the schedule will start.)
Step 2. 1. Schedule Start Date: Set the date this schedule begins. (Where: Configure Weekly Schedule -> 1. Schedule Start Date. The schedule applies from this date onwards. The previous schedule stays in the history, so past weeks are still shown as they actually were.. Result: The header shows the start date you chose.)
Step 3. 2. Regular Shift: Choose the shift the employee normally works. Each option shows the shift name and its hours. If the employee works more than one shift in a day, use **Add Another Shift**. (Where: Configure Weekly Schedule -> 2. Regular Shift. The regular shift is applied to every day that is not a rest day and has not been given its own shift.. Result: The chosen shift and its hours are shown underneath the selector.)
Step 4. 3. Rest Day(s): Select each day that is a rest day. Selected days are marked "Rest day"; the others read "Working". You may select more than one, or none. (Where: Configure Weekly Schedule -> 3. Rest Day(s). A rest day is part of the schedule. It is not leave, and it does not use any leave credit.. Result: The weekly preview updates as you select days.)
Step 5. 4. Weekly Preview, then save: Check the seven-day preview. Each day reads Working with its shift, Rest Day, or Needs Setup. Use **Customise** on any day that should differ. If anything is still unresolved, the window lists it before you can save. When it is right, select **Save Weekly Schedule**. (Where: Configure Weekly Schedule -> Save Weekly Schedule. Warning: If the save button is unavailable, read the note underneath it — it names exactly what still needs attention.. Result: A confirmation appears and the Schedule tab shows the new week, with the change added to the schedule history.)
What happens next: The schedule is used by attendance monitoring from the start date. The previous schedule remains in the history for earlier dates.
Problem: The save button is greyed out. — Solution: Look at the note beneath it and the list above. Usually one or more working days still need a shift chosen.
Problem: A day shows "Needs Setup". — Solution: That day is neither a rest day nor assigned a shift. Use Customise to give it a shift, or mark it as a rest day.
Problem: It says two shifts overlap. — Solution: Two shifts on the same day cover the same hours. Choose shifts that do not overlap.
Problem: There are no shifts to choose. — Solution: Add the shift to the Shift Catalog first — that is HR Personnel only.
Tip: Use the start date to plan ahead: set a future date and the new pattern takes effect on that day by itself.
Tip: The History tab on Work Schedule shows who changed a schedule and when.

entries.title: How to Use the Holiday Calendar
entries.text:
See the days Hospicio observes as holidays or non-working days, and (HR) keep the calendar up to date.
Purpose: Know which dates are holidays, special non-working days, organisation non-working days or suspensions.
Before you start: You are signed in. The calendar is kept up to date by HR.
Step 1. Open the calendar: In the menu, open **Attendance** and select **Holiday Calendar**. (Where: Left menu -> Attendance -> Holiday Calendar. Result: The entries for the year are listed.)
Step 2. Read an entry: Each entry shows its date, name, type, status and **Who Works** — the units HR marked as working that day. Every other unit observes it. (Where: Holiday Calendar -> list. Result: You know whether your unit works on that day.)
What happens next: For staff in a working unit, their normal schedule stands that day and they are not counted as on holiday.
Problem: A holiday is missing. — Solution: Ask HR — only HR can change the calendar.
Tip: A holiday is not a rest day or leave — the three are recorded separately.

entries.title: How Attendance Is Imported (Mustard Seedtime Export)
entries.text:
How attendance reaches HRISense from the biometric export, and what "No imported record" means.
Purpose: Explain where attendance records come from, how HR imports them, and why some dates show no data.
When to use: When you are wondering why a date shows no attendance data, or how the attendance import works.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel or a Supervisor. Only HR Personnel can import.
Step 1. Understand the chain: Staff record their time on the biometric device. HR exports the Mustard Seedtime Timesheet Report (an Excel .xls file) and imports it into HRISense. HRISense is not connected to the device directly. (Each person in the export is matched by their timekeeping code, never by name.. Result: You know which step produces the data HRISense shows.)
Step 2. Upload the export (HR): Open **Daily Monitoring**, select the **Import** tab, then select **Upload export** and choose the file. (Where: Attendance -> Daily Monitoring -> Import -> Upload export. Uploading changes nothing on its own. HRISense reads the file and compares every employee-day with what it already holds.. Result: The import appears in Import history with a review list of every row.)
Step 3. Review what was held back (HR): Rows that differ from a record already on file, carry a warning flag (for example a punch outside the schedule, or a name that does not match the code), or belong to an unknown code wait for you. Choose **Use file** or **Keep record** on each. (Where: Import -> review list. Warning: A record HR corrected by hand is kept unless you deliberately choose Use file.. Result: Every row that could write has a decision.)
Step 4. Apply the import (HR): Select **Apply import**. Only the rows you accepted are written. (Where: Import -> Apply import. Result: Attendance for the imported period appears in Daily Monitoring and the Attendance Tally.)
What happens next: Days the export does not cover — or days with no punches — stay without a record. "No imported record" means no data was received for that day. It is never an absence.
Problem: A whole period shows no attendance. — Solution: The export for that period has not been imported yet. Supervisors: raise it with HR. It is not a fault in the monitoring screens.
Problem: Apply import is refused. — Solution: Some rows still need a decision. Filter the review list and choose Use file or Keep record for each.
Problem: A code in the file matches nobody. — Solution: HR maps the code to the right employee (the screen suggests the closest name), or the row is skipped.
Tip: HRISense records attendance hours only. Pay is calculated outside HRISense.

entries.title: How to Maintain the Holiday Calendar (HR)
entries.text:
Approve fetched public holidays, add your own entries, mark units that work, and retire old entries.
Purpose: Keep the organisation's holidays and non-working days correct, so attendance, schedules and imports treat them properly.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.
Step 1. Fetch and approve public holidays: On **Holiday Calendar**, fetch the suggestions for the year. The year's Philippine holidays are added as **Pending**; **Approve** each one that applies, or **Ignore** it. (Where: Holiday Calendar -> fetch suggestions -> Approve / Ignore. Result: Approved holidays are in force.)
Step 2. Add your own entries: Add a holiday, special non-working day, organisation non-working day or suspension that the list does not have. Edit it later if it changes. (Where: Holiday Calendar -> add entry. Result: Your entry is created already approved.)
Step 3. Mark the units that work: Open **Working units** on an entry and tick the units expected to work that day (for example Pastoral Care / Homelife Services). (Where: Holiday Calendar -> Working units. For staff in those units the entry does not apply: their normal schedule stands and they are not counted as on holiday.. Result: **Who Works** shows those units; all others observe the day.)
Step 4. Retire an entry: Deactivate an entry that no longer applies and confirm. (Where: Holiday Calendar -> deactivate. Result: It stops applying to attendance; the record is kept for history.)
What happens next: Approved entries appear on Daily Monitoring, schedule coverage, the dashboard calendar and in import checks. Every change is kept in the schedule history.
Problem: It says an entry with this date and name already exists. — Solution: Edit the existing entry instead of adding it again.
Tip: Nothing is pre-set: every unit observes an entry until you mark it as working.

entries.title: How to File a Leave Request
entries.text:
Ask for leave, choosing the type, the dates and the reason.
Purpose: Submit a leave request so it can be endorsed and decided.
When to use: Whenever you need time off, as far in advance as you can.
Before you start: You are signed in to HRISense.; You know the type of leave and the dates.
Step 1. Open the request form: In the menu on the left, open **Leave Management** and select **New Request**. (Where: Left menu -> Leave Management -> New Request. Result: The leave request form opens.)
Step 2. Check your employee information: The **Employee Information** block shows your name, position, date employed and unit / department from your record — you do not type them. HR Personnel can file on behalf of another employee, or for several employees at once, under **Request For**. (Where: New Request -> Request For. If something in your employee information is wrong, ask HR to correct your record.. Result: Your details are shown at the top of the form.)
Step 3. Choose the type, dates and details: Choose the **Leave Type** — grouped as on Hospicio's paper form (VL, SL/EL, BL, Paternity / Maternity, Leave Without Pay, Others / Offset / Solo Parent). Set the **Start Date** and **End Date**; the **Total Number of Leave Applied** is worked out for you. Write the **Reason**, and add your **Address During Leave** and **Contact Number** (your mobile is filled in; change it if you will use another). (Where: New Request -> Leave Type, Start Date, End Date, Reason. Tip: Check the **Leave Record** — Total Available, Less: This Leave, Balance After Leave — before you submit. You can still file for more than you have; your head and HR decide, and may approve fewer days.. Result: The form shows the type, dates, total days, reason and your leave record.)
Step 4. Submit: Submit the request. (Where: New Request -> submit. Result: A confirmation appears and the request is listed under Leave Requests as **Waiting for head** (or **Waiting for HR** if you have no assigned head).)
What happens next: Your head / supervisor reviews it first — they may endorse it, propose a change (other dates or fewer days), or decline it. HR Personnel then make the final decision and may approve it as requested, approve the proposed change, or approve other dates. Open the request to see its stage, what was proposed, and — if it changed — your original request beside the final approved leave. You are notified at each step.
Problem: The dates are refused. — Solution: Check that the end date is not before the start date, and that the dates are not already covered by another request.
Problem: My request still says Waiting for head after several days. — Solution: Your head has not acted on it yet. Follow it up with them. You can also cancel it from the request while it is still waiting.
Problem: I need leave for a day that is already my rest day. — Solution: A rest day is already a non-working day, so no leave is needed for it. Ask HR if you are unsure how your week is set up.
Tip: File as early as you can — units need time to arrange cover.
Tip: Leave is not the same as a rest day. Rest days come from your weekly schedule.

entries.title: How to Check Your Leave Requests
entries.text:
See where each of your requests has reached.
Purpose: Follow a leave request from filing to decision.
When to use: After filing a request, or when you need to check a past one.
Before you start: You are signed in to HRISense.
Step 1. Open Leave Requests: In the menu on the left, open **Leave Management** and select **Leave Requests**. (Where: Left menu -> Leave Management -> Leave Requests. Result: Your requests are listed with their type, dates and status.)
Step 2. Read the stage: Each request shows its stage in plain words: **Waiting for head** (or **Waiting for HR** if you have no head), **Endorsed — with HR**, **Change proposed — with HR**, **Approved**, **Approved with changes**, **Declined** or **Cancelled**. Select **View** to open the full request. (Where: Leave Requests -> My Requests -> View. The request shows a stage tracker, your leave record for that type, any change your head proposed, the reason if it was declined, and its history.. Result: You can see exactly where the request is and who has acted on it.)
What happens next: You are notified when the status changes. Approved leave appears on the leave calendar.
Problem: My request was declined and I do not know why. — Solution: Open the request — the reason is shown with the decision.
Problem: I cannot see a request I filed. — Solution: Check any status filter on the page, then look again. Cancelled requests may be hidden by the default view.
Tip: The bell icon at the top right also tells you when a decision has been made.

entries.title: How to Cancel a Leave Request
entries.text:
Withdraw a request you no longer need.
Purpose: Withdraw a leave request so it is no longer waiting for a decision.
When to use: When your plans change and you no longer need the leave.
Before you start: You are signed in.; The request has not already been decided in a way that prevents cancelling.
Step 1. Open the request: Go to **Leave Management** -> **Leave Requests** and select the request. (Where: Leave Requests -> request. Result: The request details open.)
Step 2. Cancel it: Select **Cancel request** and confirm. This is possible only while the request is still waiting for a decision. (Where: Request -> cancel. Cancelling releases any days that were being held against your balance while the request was awaiting a decision.. Result: The request shows as **Cancelled** and is no longer waiting on anyone.)
What happens next: The request stays in your list as cancelled, so the history is preserved.
Problem: There is no cancel action. — Solution: The request may already be decided. Speak to HR Personnel if approved leave needs to be undone.
Tip: Cancel as soon as you know, so your supervisor is not reviewing something that is no longer needed.

entries.title: How to Read Your Leave Balances
entries.text:
Understand the total, used, pending and remaining figures.
Purpose: See how much leave of each type is recorded for you.
When to use: Before filing a request, or when checking a figure with HR.
Before you start: You are signed in.
Step 1. Open your leave balances: Open **My Profile** and select **Leave**. Your dashboard's **Your Leave Balances** panel shows the same available figures. (Where: My Profile -> Leave. Result: A table shows each leave type recorded for you, by year.)
Step 2. Read the columns: The columns are **Year**, **Leave type**, **Total**, **Source**, **Used**, **Pending**, **Forfeited** and **Available**. Above them, **Entitlement by completed years of service** shows your start date, your completed years and what each leave type gives you. (Where: Leave Balances table. Pending is days held for requests that have been filed but not yet decided. Available is what is left once used, pending and forfeited days are taken off the total. Source says whether the total follows your completed years (Automatic) or was entered by HR.. Vacation: 0 days before your first completed year, 10 days from 1 completed year, 15 from 3. Sick: 7 and Bereavement: 5 from 1 completed year. Paternity and Solo Parent: 7 from 1 completed year, only if HR has marked you eligible. A year is completed on the anniversary of your start date.. Result: You can see what is available for each leave type.)
What happens next: Filing a request moves days into Pending; a decision then moves them to Used or releases them.
Problem: No balances are listed. — Solution: Automatic balances start after your first completed year of service. For other leave types, HR records the balance — contact HR Personnel.
Problem: A figure does not match my own record. — Solution: Raise it with HR Personnel — balances are maintained by HR.
Tip: Check your balance before filing, so you are not surprised by the decision.

entries.title: How to Set an Employee's Leave Balances
entries.text:
Record or correct the leave credits an employee has for a year.
Purpose: Check the automatic entitlement, and record or correct the leave credits that are entered by HR.
When to use: When an employee joins, for leave types without an automatic entitlement, or when a correction is agreed.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; Vacation, Sick, Bereavement, Paternity and Solo Parent leave are calculated from completed years of service; you only enter other leave types or deliberate exceptions.
Step 1. Open the employee's balances: Open the employee's 201 profile and select the **Leave Balances** tab. (Where: Employee profile -> Leave Balances. Result: The balances already recorded are listed by year and leave type.)
Step 2. Add or change a balance: Choose the **Year** and the **Leave type**, then enter the total and, if applicable, any forfeited days. (Where: Leave Balances -> add / edit. Warning: A total you enter is marked as entered by HR and the automatic entitlement will not change it. To go back to the policy figure, use **Use policy** in the entitlement table. Used and pending days are maintained by HRISense from actual requests.. Result: The form holds the figures you entered.)
Step 3. Save: Save the balance. (Where: Leave Balances -> save. Result: The table shows the new figures, and the employee sees them on their own profile.)
What happens next: The employee's requests are measured against the recorded balance, and the remaining figure updates as requests are decided.
Problem: The remaining figure is not what I expected. — Solution: Remaining is the total less used, pending and forfeited days. Check whether the employee has requests awaiting a decision.
Problem: An employee has no balances at all. — Solution: Automatic balances are created once the employee has a completed year of service (Paternity and Solo Parent only if marked eligible). Use **Update leave entitlements** on the Leave page to apply them to everyone now. Other leave types are added by HR.
Problem: The policy figure and the balance differ. — Solution: The balance was entered by HR, so it is kept. Select **Use policy** in the entitlement table if it should follow the completed-years entitlement instead.
Tip: Record balances per year, so the previous year's figures stay intact.

entries.title: How to Endorse, Propose a Change to, or Decline a Team Member's Leave
entries.text:
Review your team's leave requests and recommend them to HR — as filed, or with a proposed change.
Purpose: Give your view on a team member's leave request before HR makes the final decision.
When to use: When one of your direct reports files leave.
Before you start: You are signed in as a Supervisor.; The employee is recorded as reporting to you.
Step 1. Open Leave Requests: In the menu on the left, open **Leave Management** and select **Leave Requests**. (Where: Left menu -> Leave Management -> Leave Requests. Result: Requests from your team are listed, with **Pending** ones waiting on you.)
Step 2. Review the request: Select **View** on a request. One screen shows the employee (position, unit, date employed, years of service), the leave type, dates, total days, reason, address and contact during leave, and the **Leave Record** — total available, less this leave, balance after. (Where: Leave Requests -> request. Result: The full request opens in a panel.)
Step 3. Endorse, propose a change, or decline: Select **Endorse to HR** to recommend it as filed (a note to HR is optional). If other dates or fewer days would work better, select **Propose a change**, set the **From** and **To**, give the reason, and select **Endorse with this change**. Select **Decline** only if it cannot be supported, and give the reason. (Where: Request panel -> Endorse to HR / Propose a change / Decline. Neither endorsing nor proposing approves the leave — HR decides. A proposal does not change the employee's request: HR sees both and chooses. The employee is told what you proposed.. Warning: Declining ends the request, so the reason you give is what the employee will read. Most disagreements are better handled with **Propose a change**.. Result: The status becomes **Endorsed — with HR** or **Change proposed — with HR**, or **Declined** with your reason.)
What happens next: Endorsed requests go to HR Personnel. The employee is notified of each change.
Problem: A team member says they filed leave but I cannot see it. — Solution: You only see requests from staff recorded as reporting to you. Ask HR Personnel to check the supervisor assignment on their record.
Problem: I endorsed by mistake. — Solution: Contact HR Personnel before they decide — they can still reject the request.
Tip: Endorse promptly. A request left pending is waiting on you, not on HR.

entries.title: How to Approve, Revise or Decline a Leave Request
entries.text:
Make the final decision on a leave request as HR Personnel — as requested, as the head proposed, or with other dates.
Purpose: Decide leave requests, so employees and units know where they stand.
When to use: When requests are waiting, particularly those endorsed by a supervisor.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.
Step 1. Open Leave Requests: In the menu on the left, open **Leave Management** and select **Leave Requests**. Look for requests marked **Endorsed — with HR** or **Change proposed — with HR**. (Where: Left menu -> Leave Management -> Leave Requests. You can also decide a request that is still Pending, but usually the supervisor endorses it first.. Result: Requests are listed with their status.)
Step 2. Review it: Select **View**. One screen shows the employee and their years of service, the request, the head's note and any **change proposed** by the head, the **Leave Record** (including the balance if the proposal is approved), and the history. (Where: Leave Requests -> request. Result: The full request opens.)
Step 3. Decide: Select **Approve** (or **Approve as requested**) to grant what was filed; **Approve proposed change** to grant the head's dates; or **Approve other dates** to set your own From / To with a reason. Select **Decline** and give the reason if it cannot be granted. (Where: Request panel -> Approve / Approve proposed change / Approve other dates / Decline. When the approved leave differs, the employee's original request is kept and shown beside the final approved leave, with the reason. The balance is charged the final days, never the original ones.. Warning: The decision is final in HRISense and the employee is notified.. Result: The request shows as **Approved**, **Approved with changes** or **Declined**, and the employee's balance is updated.)
What happens next: Approved leave appears on the leave calendar and in the leave report. The employee is notified either way.
Problem: The employee has no balance for that leave type. — Solution: Record the balance on their Leave Balances tab first, then decide the request.
Problem: I approved the wrong request. — Solution: Speak to the employee and their supervisor. Corrections should be recorded openly rather than quietly reversed.
Tip: Check the leave calendar before approving, so a unit is not left short.

entries.title: How to Use the Leave Calendar
entries.text:
See who is on leave on which dates before deciding or planning.
Purpose: See leave laid out across the month rather than as a list.
When to use: Before approving leave, before filing your own, or when planning cover.
Before you start: You are signed in to HRISense.
Step 1. Open the calendar: In the menu on the left, open **Leave Management** and select **Leave Calendar**. (Where: Left menu -> Leave Management -> Leave Calendar. What you see depends on your role: HR Personnel see the whole hospital, supervisors see their team, and employees see their own leave.. Result: The month opens with leave marked on the relevant dates.)
Step 2. Read a date: Select a date to see who is on leave that day and what type it is. (Where: Leave Calendar -> date. Result: The people on leave that day are listed.)
What happens next: You can move straight to filing a request for dates you have identified as free.
Problem: Approved leave is not shown. — Solution: Check you are looking at the right month, and that any filters are cleared.
Tip: Rest days are not shown here — they belong to the weekly schedule, not to leave.

entries.title: How to Create an Evaluation Form Template
entries.text:
Use Hospicio's official forms, or define your own criteria, rating scale and weights.
Purpose: Set up the form that evaluators fill in, so every evaluation asks the same questions.
When to use: Before launching an evaluation cycle, or when the appraisal criteria change.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; The criteria and their weighting have been agreed.
Step 1. Open the templates list: In the menu on the left, select **Evaluations**, then open the **Evaluation Templates** tab. (Where: Left menu -> Evaluations -> Evaluation Templates. Hospicio de San Jose’s official forms — Eval Form 1 to 4 and the Simplified Evaluation for Coordinators, Supervisors, and Heads — are listed first and marked **Official · Hospicio de San Jose**. They can be viewed and used, never edited: select **View**, then **Duplicate as Custom** to make your own version. Your own templates are marked **Custom**.. Result: Existing templates are listed with their rating method, number of review areas or criteria, and status.)
Step 2. Create the template: Select **New Template**. Give it a name and choose the rating method — each card shows the exact answers evaluators will choose from, and the **Rating Scale** below it lists them. Add flat **Criteria**, or **Review areas with statements** like the Hospicio forms. With **Weighted Scoring** on, press **Auto-Distribute to 100%** to share the weights equally, then adjust any of them; the total must read **100% / 100% · Ready** before you can save. Optionally tick **Used for job roles** so employees in those roles are always evaluated with this template. (Where: Templates -> Create Template. Tip: Write criteria in plain language — the people filling in the form are not always HR staff. Auto-Distribute is an HRISense convenience: Hospicio’s paper forms print no weights.. Result: The template form holds all your criteria.)
Step 3. Save and manage: Save the template. Use the edit action to change one, or deactivate a template that should no longer be used. (Where: Templates -> Save / Edit / Deactivate. Warning: Changing a template does not change evaluations already completed with it.. Result: The template appears in the list and can be chosen when creating a cycle.)
What happens next: The template can now be selected when you create an evaluation cycle.
Problem: I cannot deactivate a template. — Solution: It may be in use by an active cycle. Close the cycle first.
Tip: Keep the number of criteria manageable — long forms get rushed.

entries.title: How to Create and Run an Evaluation Cycle
entries.text:
Open a review period, choose who is evaluated, and close it when finished.
Purpose: Run a round of evaluations as a **Standard Evaluation** (the head / supervisor / coordinator evaluates the employee) or a **Weighted Multi-Rater Evaluation** (self 20% + peer 20% + head 60%). Either way the head discusses it with the employee, then HR finalises.
When to use: At the start of each appraisal period.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; An active evaluation template exists.
Step 1. Open the cycles list: Select **Evaluations** in the menu on the left and open **Evaluation Cycles**. The summary cards show Employees Under Review, Not Started, In Progress, Head Evaluation Submitted and Completed. (Where: Left menu -> Evaluations -> Evaluation Cycles. Result: You can see the state of every current cycle at a glance.)
Step 2. Create the cycle: Select **New Evaluation Cycle**. First choose the **Evaluation Type**: **Standard Evaluation** or **Weighted Multi-Rater Evaluation** (the chosen card is marked **Selected**). Give the cycle a name, choose the **Form Template** (and, for an official form, its **Nature of Appraisal** / **Type of Evaluation**), set the period it covers, choose which employees it applies to, and how the head / supervisor / coordinator is first chosen (immediate supervisor, one evaluator, or manual). The last step lists **Templates that will be used** — employees whose job role has its own template (for example Maintenance Staff → Eval Form 1) get that one. (Where: Cycles -> Create Cycle. **Standard:** only the head / supervisor / coordinator rates — no self rating, no peer rating. Each review area's average, the overall result and its percentage are calculated automatically (for example **4.13 / 5 · 82.6%**). **Weighted Multi-Rater:** the employee rates themselves, the peers you select rate them, and the head rates them; the final result is **self 20% + peer 20% + head 60%** — Hospicio's official weighting, which cannot be changed. Several peers share the one 20% (their scores are averaged first). The result reads like **4.33 / 5 · Equivalent 86.6%**, with each component shown. The type cannot be changed after the cycle is created.. Warning: HR and other full-access administrators (including Sister) are not offered as the **Designated Evaluator**: HR administers evaluations and does not rate.. Result: The cycle form holds the template, the period and the scope.)
Step 3. Choose the evaluators: Open the cycle. For each employee select **Evaluators** to assign or change the **head / supervisor / coordinator** and — in a Weighted Multi-Rater cycle — to add **peer evaluators**, from a unit you choose or individually. Only the people you tick are added. (Where: Evaluations -> Cycles -> cycle -> Evaluators. Each employee row shows the head evaluation, the Discussion and HR finalization (and, in a weighted cycle, Self rating and Peer evaluations, x of y completed). HR manages who evaluates but never enters ratings: you cannot pick yourself, HR and Sister are never peers, and they are the head only of their own direct reports.. Result: Every employee has a head evaluator, and (weighted cycles) the peers you chose are listed.)
Step 4. Close the cycle when finished: When all evaluations are finalised, close the cycle. (Where: Cycles -> Close Evaluation Cycle. Warning: Closing stops further evaluations being submitted for that period.. Result: The cycle status becomes closed and it moves out of the active list.)
What happens next: Evaluators complete their assignments, then HR finalises each one.
Problem: An employee has no assignment. — Solution: Check the cycle scope — they may not be included, or they may have joined after the cycle was created.
Problem: An employee shows "Not assigned" for the head evaluation. — Solution: The employee had no supervisor (or the cycle used Manual Assignment). Select **Evaluators** on their row and choose the head / supervisor / coordinator.
Tip: The summary cards are the quickest way to see how far along a cycle is.

entries.title: How to Complete an Evaluation You Have Been Assigned
entries.text:
Your self rating, a peer evaluation, or a head evaluation: fill it in, save a draft, submit — and, as head, record the discussion.
Purpose: Record your assessment against the agreed criteria — of yourself (self rating), of a colleague HR asked you to rate (peer evaluation), or of someone you lead (head / supervisor / coordinator evaluation).
When to use: When an evaluation has been assigned to you during an active cycle.
Before you start: You are signed in.; An evaluation has been assigned to you. Only the assigned evaluator can rate — HR does not rate on anyone's behalf.
Step 1. Find your assignment: Select **Evaluations** in the menu on the left and open **My Evaluations**. The **Your Part** column says whether each is your self rating, a peer evaluation or a head evaluation. (Where: Left menu -> Evaluations -> My Evaluations. Result: Your assignments are listed with the employee, your part and the cycle.)
Step 2. Start the evaluation: Select **Start Evaluation** on the assignment. (Where: Assignment -> Start Evaluation. Result: The evaluation form opens with the criteria from the template.)
Step 3. Fill it in and save a draft: Rate each statement — the choices show their number and meaning (for example **4 — Very Good**), and the rating scale stays visible at the top with your progress (**18 of 39 items answered**). Add comments, the general comments and, on Hospicio’s Forms 1–4, the **Goals and Objectives**. Save as a draft at any point if you need to come back to it. (Where: Evaluation form -> save draft. Tip: Comments are as valuable as the ratings — write what you actually observed.. Result: The assignment shows as In Progress and your work is kept.)
Step 4. Submit: When it is complete, select **Review & Submit**. Check the summary — answered and unanswered items, comments and the calculated score — then select **Submit Evaluation**. (Where: Evaluation form -> Submit Evaluation. Warning: You can **Reopen to edit** until HR finalises — for a head evaluation, only until the discussion is recorded.. Result: The assignment shows as **Submitted**.)
Step 5. Head evaluator: record the discussion: After submitting a head evaluation, discuss it with the employee. Then open it again (**Record Discussion**), enter the **Discussion date** and **Discussion notes**, and select **Mark discussion completed**. (Where: Evaluation form -> Discussion with the evaluated employee. Warning: HR cannot finalise the evaluation until the discussion is recorded. After it is recorded your ratings are locked.. Result: The evaluation shows the discussion as Completed with its date.)
What happens next: When the head evaluation and the discussion are complete — and, in a Weighted Multi-Rater cycle, the self rating and every selected peer evaluation — HR Personnel finalise it. The employee then sees the result if HR made it visible; peer ratings are never shown to them.
Problem: Submit is unavailable. — Solution: Every statement must be rated first. The form says how many are left and marks each one **Not rated yet**.
Problem: I need to change something after submitting. — Solution: Open it and select **Reopen to edit**, then submit again. This is not possible once HR has finalised it, or — for a head evaluation — once the discussion is recorded.
Tip: Save a draft if you are interrupted — nothing is lost.

entries.title: How to Finalise a Submitted Evaluation
entries.text:
Review a submitted evaluation and record it against the employee.
Purpose: Complete the evaluation process so the result becomes part of the employee's record.
When to use: When an employee's row in the cycle shows **Ready to finalize**.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; The head evaluation is submitted and the head has recorded the discussion with the employee. In a Weighted Multi-Rater cycle, the self rating and every selected peer evaluation are submitted too.
Step 1. Find submitted evaluations: Open **Evaluations**, open the cycle, and filter by **Ready for HR**. (Where: Evaluations -> Cycles -> cycle -> Ready for HR. Result: The employees whose evaluations are complete are listed.)
Step 2. Review the evaluation: Select **Review & finalize** on the employee's row. The head evaluation opens with the result — **Result — Standard Evaluation** (area averages, overall, %) or **Final rating** (self, peer and head with their 20 / 20 / 60 contributions). In a weighted cycle the workflow panel lists each component; use **View** to read the self rating and each peer evaluation. (Where: Assignment -> evaluation. Warning: HR does not rate and cannot change ratings. If something needs correcting, the evaluator reopens their own rating.. Result: You have read the full evaluation.)
Step 3. Finalise: Select **Finalize Evaluation** and decide whether the employee may see it. (Where: Evaluation -> Finalize. Result: The evaluation shows as Completed. If HR made it visible, the employee sees the head evaluation on their Evaluations tab.)
What happens next: The employee can see the finalised evaluation on their own profile.
Problem: An evaluation has been submitted with an obvious error. — Solution: Speak to the evaluator before finalising. Corrections come from the person who made the assessment (Reopen to edit).
Problem: Finalize is not available. — Solution: The panel lists what is missing — the head evaluation or the discussion (and, in a weighted cycle, a self rating or a peer evaluation). A peer who will not submit can be removed under **Evaluators**.
Problem: It says another HR administrator must finalize it. — Solution: You cannot finalise your own evaluation, or one you rated as a head. Another HR administrator — or Sister — finalises it.
Tip: Finalise promptly so employees receive their feedback while it is still current.

entries.title: How to Read Your Own Evaluation
entries.text:
See the evaluations that have been finalised for you.
Purpose: Read the feedback recorded about your performance.
When to use: After you are told an evaluation cycle has been completed.
Before you start: You are signed in.; An evaluation for you has been finalised.
Step 1. Open your profile: Open **My Profile** (left menu, or your name at the top right), then select **Evaluations**. (Where: My Profile -> Evaluations. Result: Your finalised evaluations are listed by cycle.)
Step 2. Open an evaluation: Select an evaluation to read the ratings and comments. (Where: Evaluations tab -> evaluation. Only your finalised head / supervisor / coordinator evaluation appears here, once HR has made it visible. Your own self rating is under Evaluations → My Evaluations; peer ratings of you are not shown.. Result: The full evaluation opens.)
What happens next: Discuss anything you disagree with with your supervisor or HR Personnel.
Problem: My evaluation is not there. — Solution: It has not been finalised yet. Ask HR Personnel when it is expected.
Tip: Evaluations stay on your record, so you can look back at previous cycles.

entries.title: How to Create a Training or Seminar
entries.text:
Record an activity — what, when, who attends — and optionally link it to a compliance requirement.
Purpose: Record a training activity and the staff expected to attend it.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; You know the provider, venue, dates and who should attend.
Step 1. Start a new activity: Open **Training & Seminars** and select **Create Training / Seminar**. Enter the title, the type (Training, Seminar, Workshop, Orientation, Conference or Other), the provider / facilitator and the venue. (Where: Training & Seminars -> Create Training / Seminar. Result: Step 1 is complete.)
Step 2. Set when it happens: Set the start and end dates and times, the **Hours Credit**, the **Capacity**, and — if completing it satisfies a compliance requirement — choose it under **Compliance Link**. Otherwise leave **None / Standalone Training**. (Where: Activity form -> When / Compliance Link. With a compliance link, marking a participant Completed records their compliance for that requirement automatically.. Result: Step 2 is complete.)
Step 3. Choose who attends: Filter the employee list and tick the people who should attend, or use **Select Matches** to add everyone in the filter. (Where: Activity form -> Who should attend?. Result: The participant list is built.)
Step 4. Review and save: Check the summary and save. (Where: Activity form -> Review. Result: The activity is created with its participants.)
What happens next: After the session, record each participant's outcome.
Problem: The compliance requirement I want is not listed. — Solution: Create the requirement in Compliance first, then link it.
Tip: You can add more participants later from the activity itself.

entries.title: How to Add Participants to a Training
entries.text:
Add more staff to an activity that already exists.
Purpose: Add staff to an activity after it was created.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; The activity exists.
Step 1. Open the activity: In **Training & Seminars**, open the activity. (Where: Training & Seminars -> activity. Result: The activity shows its details, **Total Assigned** and the participant list.)
Step 2. Add participants: Select **Add Participants**, choose the employees and confirm. (Where: Activity -> Add Participants. Compare **Total Assigned** with the capacity. The figure can go over 100% — HRISense shows it rather than hiding it.. Result: They are added to the participant list as Assigned.)
What happens next: After the session, record each participant's outcome.
Problem: An employee is not in the list. — Solution: Only active employees can be added. Check whether the record is archived.
Tip: Add participants early so supervisors can plan cover.

entries.title: How to Record Participation and Upload Certificates
entries.text:
Set each participant's outcome, attach certificates, and let completion update compliance.
Purpose: Record what actually happened for each participant, and keep their certificate on file.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; The activity has participants.
Step 1. Set an outcome: Open the activity and use **Update Participant Outcome** on a participant: choose **Completed**, **Did Not Attend**, **Excused** or **Cancelled**, and add the completion date, **Valid Until** date and notes where they apply. To update several people at once, select them first. (Where: Activity -> Update Participant Outcome. Warning: Record what actually happened. Marking someone Completed when they did not attend puts a false record on their file.. Result: The participant shows the new outcome.)
Step 2. Attach the certificate: Select **Upload Certificate** for a participant and choose the file with **Select Certificate File**. Use it again to replace a certificate. (Where: Activity -> Upload Certificate. Result: The certificate can be downloaded by HR and by the participant.)
Step 3. Check the compliance link: If the activity is linked to a compliance requirement, a participant marked **Completed** automatically gets an **Accepted** compliance record for it, valid until the date you entered. (Where: Compliance. Result: Their compliance standing updates.)
What happens next: Employees see their own outcome and certificate on **My Profile** → **Training**.
Problem: The compliance record did not appear. — Solution: Check that the activity is linked to the requirement and that the participant is marked Completed.
Tip: Use **Upload Activity Document** to keep the materials with the activity (HR only).

entries.title: How to See Trainings and Your Own Training History
entries.text:
Browse training activities and check what you were assigned, completed and certified for.
Purpose: See the activities on offer and your own record of them.
Before you start: You are signed in.
Step 1. Browse activities: Select **Training & Seminars** in the menu. Search and filter the activities, and open one to read its details. (Where: Left menu -> Training & Seminars. You see the activities and their totals, but only your own participant row — not who else was assigned.. Result: You see what is scheduled and completed.)
Step 2. Check your own history: Open **My Profile** → **Training** to see your outcome for each activity, and select **Download Certificate** where one is attached. (Where: My Profile -> Training. Result: Your training record and certificates are listed.)
What happens next: Completed training linked to a compliance requirement also counts on your **Compliance** section.
Problem: A training I attended is not listed. — Solution: Ask HR to check that you were added and marked Completed.
Problem: My certificate is missing. — Solution: Certificates are uploaded by HR. Contact HR with the activity name and date.
Tip: Upcoming trainings you are part of also appear on your dashboard calendar.

entries.title: How to Nominate and Vote for Awards
entries.text:
Nominate a colleague for Employee of the Quarter and cast your ballot for Hospicio's recognition awards.
Purpose: Take part in Hospicio's awards: nominate colleagues and vote, privately and once.
When to use: When HR opens nominations or voting.
Before you start: You are signed in to HRISense.
Step 1. Open Awards & Recognition: Select **Awards & Recognition** under Performance in the menu on the left. **Open now** lists any nominations and ballots open to you. (Where: Left menu -> Awards & Recognition. Result: You see what is open, your award history and the final results.)
Step 2. Nominate (Employee of the Quarter): In each category choose a colleague from the list — only eligible people are listed — add why if you like, and select **Nominate**. (Leadership positions (the Assistant Administrator, HR Officer, the Heads, Supervisors and Coordinators) cannot be nominated for Employee of the Quarter, but they can vote.. Result: "You nominated" shows your nomination.)
Step 3. Vote: In each category select your choice — where it says **Choose 2 different nominees**, pick two different people. Watch **Votes used / remaining**, then **Submit ballot**. (You may vote for yourself. Everyone starts at zero votes. Nobody can see whom you voted for.. Warning: A ballot is submitted once and cannot be changed.. Result: The award shows **Ballot submitted** with your own choices.)
What happens next: After voting closes, HRISense counts the votes automatically. The committee reviews and verifies the results before they are declared final; final results then appear on this page.
Problem: I cannot vote in a category. — Solution: Employee of the Quarter categories are voted on only by employees in that group. Ask HR if you think your group is wrong.
Problem: Someone is missing from the list. — Solution: They may not meet that award's rules (group, years of service, Hall of Fame, or a leadership position for Employee of the Quarter).
Tip: Vincentian and Louisian eligibility uses completed years of service, counted from your hire date.

entries.title: How to Run Awards and Recognition (HR)
entries.text:
Create award periods, map voting groups, run nomination and voting, review and declare results, and keep the Hall of Fame.
Purpose: Run each award from draft to final results. HRISense checks eligibility and counts; the committee decides.
When to use: Each quarter (Employee of the Quarter) and each year (Personnel Recognition and Awards).
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; The Voting Groups are mapped (Pastoral Care & Homelife Services starts empty).
Step 1. Map the voting groups: Open **Voting Groups**. For each group select **Edit mapping** and tick the job roles or units that belong to it, or add individual employees. Hospicio words that do not match a current job role are listed for you. (Where: Awards & Recognition -> Voting Groups. Result: Each group shows how many employees belong to it.)
Step 2. Create the award period: Open **Manage Awards** and select **Create award**: Employee of the Quarter (year and quarter), Personnel Recognition and Awards (the whole year), one official award, or a **Custom award**. Check the draft — the date years of service are counted on, the positions not eligible for Employee of the Quarter, and the Special Award titles — and **Save draft changes**. (Result: The award appears as a draft with its stages.)
Step 3. Run nomination and voting: Use the buttons in order: **Open nomination**, **Close nomination**, **Open voting**, **Close voting**. While voting is open you see turnout only. (Result: When voting closes, the automatic tally is shown.)
Step 4. Review, verify and declare: Select **Review results**. For each shortlisted result record **Confirm** (with a placement) or **Not awarded** and a note — or **Confirm all undecided** to accept the ranking. Then **Verify results** and **Declare final results**. (Warning: Final results are a permanent record and become visible to employees.. Result: The award is Finalized and appears in Award History.)
What happens next: Employees see the final results on their Awards page; awardees see the award in their own history.
Problem: Open nomination / Open voting is refused. — Solution: A category's group has nothing mapped yet. Map it under Voting Groups.
Problem: Verify results is refused. — Solution: Every shortlisted result needs a decision first.
Problem: Two nominees tie at the last Top place. — Solution: Both are kept and marked Tie at cutoff — the committee decides.
Tip: Record Hall of Fame awardees under Hall of Fame: they are then left out as Vincentian, Louisian and Special Award nominees automatically.

entries.title: How to Read Hospicio's Yearly Achievements
entries.text:
Browse the published achievement pages, one per year.
Purpose: See what Hospicio de San Jose achieved each year.
Before you start: You are signed in.
Step 1. Open Yearly Achievements: Select **Yearly Achievements** under Performance in the menu. Each published year is a card, newest first. (Where: Left menu -> Yearly Achievements. Result: The published years are listed.)
Step 2. Open a year: Select a year to read its introduction and achievements. Open any attached image or document. (Where: Yearly Achievements -> year. Result: The year's achievements are shown.)
What happens next: Pages are written by HR; new years appear once HR publishes them.
Problem: A page says "Sample content". — Solution: It is an example page HR has not replaced yet. It describes no real event or person.
Tip: Yearly Achievements are about the institution — they are not performance evaluations.

entries.title: How to Create and Publish a Yearly Achievements Page (HR)
entries.text:
Add a year, write its achievements, attach images or PDFs, and publish it.
Purpose: Keep Hospicio's record of achievements, one page per year.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.
Step 1. Create the year: On **Yearly Achievements**, select **New year** and enter the year. There is one page per year. (Where: Yearly Achievements -> New year. Result: A **Draft** page opens. Drafts are visible to HR only.)
Step 2. Write the page: Select **Edit page** to set the title, introduction and year, then **Save**. (Where: Year page -> Edit page. Result: The page shows your introduction.)
Step 3. Add achievements: Select **Add achievement**: give a title and description, and optionally attach a JPG, PNG or WEBP image or a PDF (up to 5 MB). Use the edit, **Move up**, **Move down** and **Remove** buttons on each achievement. (Where: Year page -> Add achievement. Result: The achievements appear in your chosen order.)
Step 4. Publish: Select **Publish** when the page is ready. **Unpublish** takes it back to Draft; **Delete** removes the page. (Where: Year page -> Publish. Result: Everyone signed in can now read the page.)
What happens next: Every change is recorded in the audit log.
Problem: It says a page for that year already exists. — Solution: Open the existing page and edit it instead.
Tip: The pages marked **Sample content** are examples — rewrite or delete them.

entries.title: How to Create a Compliance Requirement
entries.text:
Define something staff must hold — such as a medical exam, NCII certificate or professional license — and who it applies to.
Purpose: Record something the hospital requires staff to hold, so HRISense can track who has it.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; You know who it applies to and whether it expires. HRISense presets no expiry period.
Step 1. Name it: On **Compliance Monitoring**, select the create button to open **Create Compliance Requirement**. Optionally start from a Hospicio type — Psychological Assessment / Examination, Medical Exam, NCII Certificate — Caregiving, Professional License, or Other — then check the name and **Category** (Medical, Psychological, Certification, Professional License, Training, Document or Other). (Where: Compliance -> Create Compliance Requirement. A starting type only fills in the name and category; nobody is assigned until you choose who it applies to.. Result: Step 1 — "What requirement are you adding?" — is complete.)
Step 2. Choose who needs it: Choose **All Employees**, a **Specific Unit**, a **Specific Department**, a **Specific Role** (one or more job roles) or **Specific Employees**. For Professional License and NCII Caregiving, tick only the job roles they apply to. (Where: Create Compliance Requirement -> Who needs this requirement?. Result: Step 2 — "Who needs this requirement?" — is complete.)
Step 3. Decide whether it expires: If it must be renewed, choose that it has an expiration date and set the reminder window (how many days before expiry it shows as Expiring Soon). Otherwise choose **No expiration**. (Where: Create Compliance Requirement -> Does this requirement expire?. Result: Step 3 — "Does this requirement expire?" — is complete.)
Step 4. Review and create: Check the summary and create the requirement. (Where: Create Compliance Requirement -> Review. Result: Everyone in scope is measured against it; anyone without a record appears under **Needs Attention** as Missing.)
What happens next: Medical and Psychological requirements are fulfilled by the employee's medical or psychological records; others by compliance records, or automatically by completing a linked training.
Problem: Nobody, or the wrong people, appear against the requirement. — Solution: Check who it applies to — the scope may be narrower or wider than intended.
Problem: I no longer need a requirement. — Solution: Select **Deactivate** on it. Existing records and history are kept.
Tip: Use expiry tracking for anything renewable, so it appears before it lapses.

entries.title: How to Work the Needs Attention List
entries.text:
Find who is missing, expiring, expired or waiting for review, and act on it.
Purpose: See where staff are out of compliance and who needs following up.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; At least one active requirement exists.
Step 1. Open Compliance: Select **Compliance** in the menu. **Items Needing Attention** lists every person and requirement that needs action. (Where: Left menu -> Compliance -> Needs Attention. Result: The list is ordered Expired, Missing, Expiring Soon, Needs Review.)
Step 2. Read the reason: Each row shows its reason: **Missing** (nothing on file), **Expiring Soon** (inside the reminder window), **Expired**, or **Needs Review** (submitted but not accepted). (Where: Needs Attention -> Attention Reason. Statuses are worked out from the records each time the page opens, so they are always current.. Result: You know what each person needs.)
Step 3. Act on a row: Select **Add Record** to record a fulfilment, or **View Medical** / **View Psych** for health requirements, which are handled on the Medical and Psychological pages. (Where: Needs Attention -> Add Record / View Medical / View Psych. Result: The record is added or reviewed where it belongs.)
What happens next: The **Requirements** and **Employees** tabs show the same standing per requirement and per employee.
Problem: Somebody appears who should not be in scope. — Solution: Check who the requirement applies to.
Tip: Work Expired first, then Missing and Expiring Soon.

entries.title: How to Record an Employee's Compliance
entries.text:
Record that an employee met a requirement, with dates, notes and the evidence.
Purpose: Record that an employee has met a requirement, and keep the evidence with it.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; You have the document or reference from the employee.
Step 1. Open Record Compliance Fulfillment: Select **Add Record** on a Needs Attention row, or open the employee's profile → **Compliance** and select **Record Fulfillment**. (Where: Compliance -> Add Record / Employee profile -> Compliance -> Record Fulfillment. Result: The **Record Compliance Fulfillment** form opens.)
Step 2. Fill it in: Choose the requirement, enter the completion date and — if it expires — the valid-until date, add notes, and attach the document. (Where: Record Compliance Fulfillment. Result: The form is complete.)
Step 3. Submit: Submit the record. (Where: Record Compliance Fulfillment -> submit. The record is saved as **Pending review**, so the requirement shows as **Needs Review** for that employee.. Result: The record appears on the employee's Compliance section.)
What happens next: Medical and psychological requirements are reviewed on their own pages (**Administrative Review**). A linked training marked Completed records compliance automatically as Accepted.
Problem: The requirement I need is not listed for this employee. — Solution: It does not apply to them. Check who the requirement applies to.
Problem: A record I submitted stays at Needs Review. — Solution: HRISense does not yet have a screen for accepting general compliance records — only medical and psychological records are reviewed (on their own pages). The record stays Pending review.
Tip: Record the valid-until date accurately: it drives the Expiring Soon and Expired statuses.

entries.title: How to Check Your Own Compliance Standing
entries.text:
See which requirements apply to you and which are outstanding.
Purpose: Know what the hospital requires of you and what is still outstanding.
When to use: When you are asked to renew something, or to check before a deadline.
Before you start: You are signed in.
Step 1. Open your compliance: Select your name at the top right, choose **My Profile**, then open the **Compliance** tab. (Where: My Profile -> Compliance. Result: Each requirement that applies to you is listed with its status.)
Step 2. Read the statuses: Each requirement that applies to you shows **Compliant**, **Expiring Soon**, **Expired**, **Missing** (nothing recorded yet) or **Needs Review** (submitted, waiting for HR). (Where: Compliance tab. Result: You know what you still need to submit or renew.)
What happens next: Submit anything outstanding to HR Personnel, who record it against your file.
Problem: I submitted a document but it still shows as needing attention. — Solution: It is probably waiting for HR to review it. Allow a little time, then follow up.
Tip: Renew before the expiry date — an expired requirement affects the whole unit's standing.

entries.title: How to Record and Review a Medical Examination
entries.text:
Add an employee's medical exam, keep its documents confidential, and review it for compliance.
Purpose: Keep employees' medical examination records in one confidential place.
Before you start: You are signed in as HR Personnel.; You have the examination result.
Step 1. Add the record: Open **Medical Records** and select **Add Medical Record**. Choose the employee, enter the exam type, date and clinician or clinic, then add the record information — an optional compliance link, the valid-until date, notes and the report — and review it. (Where: Medical Records -> Add Medical Record. Warning: HR notes are for HR only. Never put clinical detail anywhere a supervisor could read it.. Result: The record is saved as **Pending review**.)
Step 2. Review it: Open the record and use **Administrative Review** to mark it **Accepted** or **Needs Correction**, with a reason. (Where: Medical record -> Administrative Review. If the record is linked to a Medical compliance requirement, its review and expiry decide the employee's compliance status.. Result: The review status updates.)
Step 3. Manage documents: Upload, download or delete the record's documents. Edit or delete the record if it was entered wrongly. (Where: Medical record -> documents. Result: Documents stay with the record and are visible to HR only.)
